title: Is There Hope for Chinese Education? None! What Does It Give Us? Nothing!
content:
I write this with no ill will. I only hope for China’s revival!

For years I’ve lived in a daze. Day after day I’ve drifted through life half asleep. I once wanted to fall in love, once wanted to do something big and spectacular, once wondered when I’d get into a Chinese university, once hoped that on the strength of my own grades I could get into high school without my family paying extra, without being a fee-paying “out-of-district” student. I used to dream about a lot of things, but every single one of them got shattered, one by one.

Chinese education, education with Chinese characteristics: not rigid, not flexible, stuck in a state where you’re neither dead nor alive. You don’t know whether to laugh or cry.

“Quality education” is a product of the post-1990 era, I guess! In my memory, Han Han’s essay “Taking a Bath in a Padded Coat” marks the beginning of the rise of quality education. Han Han, I call him our Lu Xun. He’s slowly been keeping a lower profile lately. My math teacher says he’s used up all his talent, but I don’t think so. Han Han is keeping a low profile because he’s pouring his energy into his racing career. He doesn’t speak out, doesn’t write much, doesn’t publish books. The subtext seems to be that the Communist Party wants to shut him up, and he just needs to lie low.

This kind of education, I don’t know how it’s any different from the old exam-oriented education. Just a different name? Decades of “quality,” and where has the quality gone? Exams are still exams, you still get into college based on grades and scores, everything is still exactly the same as before. So-called quality means filling in scores for your moral character, extracurricular activities and so on, on some crappy form. Those scores, heh, the power is in the teachers’ hands. China is a society that runs on personal connections and face, so all of it is fake, totally fake. As long as you have power, money and face, these little things take care of themselves. Quality education is total bullshit.

In every dynasty and every country, all education has had to cater to politics, to cater to whoever rules. It’s a truth that has never changed in a thousand years, and there’s no changing it. Why are we communist? I don’t know. Whatever the ruling party wants us to study, we have to study. Learning a second way of thinking, promoting a second way of thinking on home soil, seems to lead only to a dead end.

Education is China’s blind spot, the thing it doesn’t take seriously. But do you know? It’s education. How many people in China go through this half-dead education every year? 73 million, going through this half-dead education. Living through it is painful, but dying would be a waste. Chinese students all seem to be torn~

Let me borrow a passage Han Han wrote about education:

Here I have to bring up a topic that has nothing to do with the drought: education. After so many years of Project Hope, the education problems of central and western China still haven’t been fully solved. It’s very sad. Compulsory education, in any country, is a responsibility the go-vern-ment must fulfill, but China is an exception. Germany began implementing universal compulsory education in the 17th century, and Japan’s compulsory education enrollment rate at the end of the Meiji era was higher than China’s in 2000. So when other countries became developed countries long ago while China is still struggling toward “moderate prosperity,” don’t feel it’s unfair. It’s perfectly normal. Don’t tell me China’s national conditions are different. I don’t know how Japan, a country with a huge population, barren land and scarce resources, a country whose “Japanese national conditions” are extremely pronounced, became the world’s second-largest power. They seemed to have no reason to even become a developed country, but they did it. It’s all up to people. To those who “talk national conditions when I talk integration with the world, and talk integration with the world when I talk national conditions,” all I want to say is: your IQ is at best only good enough to help someone count the money after they’ve sold you. Likewise, with the help of Project Hope, our go-vern-ment’s investment in education ranks dead last in the world. The logic is the same: you’ve taken on the responsibility the go-vern-ment should bear, but you can’t do the go-vern-ment’s job, and so you indirectly leave children in the west unable to afford school. So the next time someone in our country tells you “our education has achieved another great success” or something like that, you shouldn’t feel happy. You should feel ashamed.

After reading this passage, you should understand what a load of crap China’s so-called education is!

Now let’s talk about politics. Shameless, fucking shameless, that’s my verdict. In politics, whatever is declared right is right, and even if it isn’t right it will become right. That’s politics, XX politics.

It’s a fact that can’t be changed: China’s unique family culture. It can’t be changed. So my view is that it’s all chaos. I came up with the term “chaotic political theory” myself. Maybe someone has proposed it before, but I’ve thought it through and added my own ideas.

Chaotic politics is politics where you can’t tell who’s right and who’s wrong, where solving the people’s problems is all for show, yet it’s also supposedly politics that listens to the people’s opinions. Everything is chaotic: blurry political boundaries, blurry political dealings, blurry ideology. That’s what I mean by “chaotic political theory.”

“Quality education” will die out someday, swept away by some XX that erupts!

Education tied to politics makes me sad. Why would an upstanding socialist country be like this? The reason is… I won’t say. I’ll stop here. In Han Han’s words: “Say too much and you die, and then they flog your corpse.”

One day in the past, I cried over certain things, but I held back the tears. None of it was worth pitying, because I know that in chaotic politics there’s nothing left to reform, unless it’s thoroughly…

I can’t do it, and I don’t want to make it my goal. I don’t want to reform Chinese education, and I don’t want to reform China’s XX either. None of that is my life goal. I once told a friend that those of us who see clearly, who have opened our eyes to the world, should make the wise choice and get away, and come back to our country when the time is right.

Every day’s classes exist only for the gaokao, the college entrance exam, just like the imperial examination system of the Sui and Tang dynasties, freezing people’s thinking so they can go pass the exams. It’s sad. Where has our nation’s creativity and way of thinking gone? It’s trapped in the spiderweb of so-called “quality education,” and yet we sit in the web, perfectly content, admiring our own handsome faces. Heh, the Qing government’s delusions of grandeur have come back to this land.

Is there hope for Chinese education? My own view: no hope. Maybe only a reform driven by students could do it, but… does it give us anything? No, still my view. Pitiful education. All I can do is sigh…

I hope China can change, and that the Chinese nation can be revived!

I hope my motherland grows prosperous and strong!

Education is the foundation of a nation!

A nation’s tragedy: when education fails, the nation is doomed!

Written by Jianfeng Yiyu on April 10, 2010

I hope someone will pay attention to this post

title: IE9 Beta Is Out!
content:
I’ve been waiting for this for ages, and I’d heard IE9 was seriously awesome, so I couldn’t wait to install it! Overall, my impression is pretty good! Why switch to IE9? Well, how do I put it… my IE8 kept crashing~ boo hoo, so it was time to switch……

Go to IE9’s official website to download the Chinese version. IE9 has now completely given up on XP users, so if you’re on XP and want to use it, your only option is to upgrade your operating system! (Portal to the download: download link)

Installation is easy~ done in a few steps, then restart after installing

I opened IE9 and it was super fast! Then of course I opened my own little blog and took a look. Very nice, nothing out of place! Absolutely perfect. IE9’s support for the Microsoft YaHei font is spot on! The rendering is suuuper good!

Next up is IE9’s tab dragging! Just like Chrome and FireFox! That was a given, of course! Heh~

Then I browsed a few websites. First I went to Bank of China’s site, since my online banking is with Bank of China. I opened my personal banking page and, uh…… the tab crashed! Mind-blowing……

So I thought about it~ well, there’s still a workaround: use IETester. I won’t go into it, just download IETester and you’re set.

IE9 starts up incredibly fast, a few seconds maybe! Suuuper quick!

But why does the IE9 logo look so much like IE6’s…… uh~ speechless…… IE9 still has quite a few bugs, so if you hate hassle, I’d suggest not trying it……

I ran into a few bugs myself, like weird, unexplained errors when writing posts in WLW…… link address tooltips that won’t go away…… and so on…… It is a Beta after all~ we can’t expect too much from it, ha…… This is just a little trial run anyway. IE9 supports CSS3 and HTML5, which is great~ I hope IE6 dies off soon and everyone gets on IE9! Haha! That’s just my wishful thinking, of course!

IE9 Beta is out! Hurry up and give it a try, everyone!

title: Written After XX: As Marx Once Said
content:
First things first: socialism is great! I must thank the country, thank the Party, thank the government, thank the Central Committee, thank the leaders, thank the leaders’ mistresses and so on for giving me the chance to say “socialism” is great!(Thanks to @Feiyan, my good buddy for the reminder, I couldn’t forget that line.) The XX here means Google+Firefox+Wordpress=G+F+W (written as G+0+W from here on), and it also means the XX Prize, among other things. Marx once said: censorship, like slavery, can never be legal, even if it has existed as law a thousand times over. Whatever Marx said is the truth, and it’s what the XX Party is supposed to do. After XX, these past few days have been anything but calm: the XX mass protests, the XX incident, the XX Prize, XXX… so much, too much. Since the internet is an open environment that’s hard to control, XX is bound to censor and block it. “Citizens of the People’s Republic of China enjoy freedom of speech, of the press, of assembly, of association, of procession and of demonstration.” - Article 35 of the Constitution. …As you can see, at certain times… XX will still XX, so this article seems to be nothing but a blank, bounced check. Most of the time, people get “talked out of it,” or some region gets XX’d, or XX. A perfectly good Gavatar avatar acceleration server got blocked, what a tragedy… I still remember the Xi Xiang plan in March, which was where my wall-climbing began. Some of those files are still on my computer, and I also dug up the black-box test report on XXX. Below is the network topology diagram. I’ll skip the written parts.

Big Brother in every country has the same hobby: expanding his power without limit in the name of national security. The CNCI that Uncle Sam uses for deep network inspection has a budget of 30 billion dollars. How many times bigger is that than G+0+W or Golden+Shield? Can’t you feel the global ghost of that Agency? The only difference is that Big Brother in our glorious nation is so clumsy and shameless that even ordinary people can see through him, while the free people of capitalist countries, in their fear, run into the arms of Big Brother’s unlimited power. The dawn of cyberpunk is still a long way off. Fighting the old pre-cyberpunk powers requires megacorps to grow faster, so Google, when you need to do evil, don’t hesitate.

So, in an age where pulling the plug on the internet is routine, tearing down G+F+W (cursing F+U+C+K G+0+W every now and then is enough), would not improve internet censorship at all. It could instead bring about real-name registration and the rise of Golden+Shield: a bunch of people who only know how to punish others and nothing about technology, yanking cables at random and putting the internet under martial law. The “General Theory” already said it: what both sides need is a dynamic balance in a state of struggle. Everyone just muddles along and keeps their distance. Netizens have their ways over the wall, and the GFW has something to report to its bosses, and that’s that. What we can do… seems to be nothing but keeping silent… Silence, silence, just as Lu Xun said: some peoples, because complaining is useless, stop even complaining, and so they become silent peoples, and slowly decline further and further… While I’m at it, a plug for my little site FeelSSH. It’s a free SSH account site, hehe, set up by me. It’s still free for now, and there may be paid SSH accounts later. If anyone wants to see that stuff, the materials I mentioned~~ you can find them at G+0+W Technical Review. You’ll need to get over the wall first to read it.

title: Oblivion Island: A Fairy-Tale World That Stays With Me
content:
This animated film came out back in ‘09, but I’m always a bit slow on these things. Yesterday I was browsing VeryCD looking for some movies to watch, saw this one in the animation section, and downloaded it to take a look~

Plot: Oblivion Island: Haruka and the Magic Mirror is about Haruka, an ordinary high school student who lost her mother when she was little and was raised by her father alone. The story begins at a shrine in Musashino. Haruka visits the shrine where she often played as a child, and by chance spots a fox secretly carrying off an old, discarded toy airplane. Following the fox, Haruka gets lost in the forest, and the fox vanishes. Suddenly she finds a puddle giving off a strange, magical aura. The moment she puts her hand in, she is pulled into a fantasy world: “Oblivion Island.” The little island is piled high with things humans have thrown away. Haruka meets the fox again. His name is Teo (voiced by Miyuki Sawashiro), and he lives on the island. Haruka is full of curiosity about this incredible world, and there she finds a little stuffed lamb she once treasured. Looking at the doll, she remembers the most important treasure of her childhood: “That’s right, when I was little, Mom gave me a hand mirror, but it went missing. Could it be here on this island?” Though Teo is extremely reluctant, he goes with Haruka to search for the lost mirror. But this is an island that humans are forbidden to enter. Haruka and Teo are careful not to be seen by the other residents, but the “Baron” still catches wind of them. Can Haruka find her hand mirror? And can she make it back to the real world?

How do I put it? Watching it really moved me. The stuffed animals and dolls I loved most, the comic books I read over and over, the colorful pebbles I picked up in the park…… where have all those once-treasured things gone? Did they slip away from you without you even noticing? This film is about the things so many people loved as kids being secretly gathered on an island nobody knows about. It says they’re “secretly” gathered there, but really, which of those things wasn’t forgotten or thrown away by people as they grew up? On “Oblivion Island,” where no humans live, the residents build their own streets out of humanity’s former “treasures.” It’s a world no one knows about, so what other wonders does this island hold? Over there, everything seems like a cartoon: no bloodshed, no war, just little scuffles and wave after wave of laughter. This animation is so warm and gentle. It all made me think back on the past. The drawings I loved have more or less all been tossed out by me, the toys I loved have vanished one by one, and the things I used to love slowly stopped interesting me. By the time I think of them again they’re gone, and only then do I realize how precious they were! We only learn to cherish things after we lose them. Only you know what’s worth cherishing to you, so go love and cherish it now! Go watch this film~ you’ll learn a lot~:)

PS: That little cotton ball is so cute~o(∩_∩)o

title: STRONG BUTTERFLY
content:
A poem for myself:

Over the vast sea

He beats his wings and flies

In the boundless sky

He gazes at the distant horizon

In the empty air

His companions are the clouds, the wind and the waves. One belief lives in his mind

I will fly, fly to that faraway shore

He grows a little tired

Slowly he sinks toward the surface of the sea

Splash……

A wave soaks his wings

He wobbles, as if about to vanish in the battering sea

He shakes out his wings

Pulls himself together

Changes his posture

And climbs high into the sky

The sea wind brushes the scales on his body

Their old brilliance has faded. He seems to have forgotten that he was once just a sturdy butterfly

Forgotten the mockery and the sneers of others. He remembers only his old dream

Today’s goal

Someday

When he gathers nectar in the gardens on the far shore

He will beat his wings and fly, happy

title: Back from Shanghai: The "Meat Expo" and a Tragic Country
content:
It’s been a day since I got back from the “Meat Expo” (as in, a World Expo packed with human flesh). I’m exhausted, really exhausted. I slept all day today and feel lousy. We took the bullet train there and the bullet train back. What I felt most at the World Expo was people, so damn many people. Not just a lot, an insane amount. I guess that’s China’s great strength!

I never used to think crowds were a bad thing, but now I really get it. This trip to the Expo really left a big impression on me. To hit its target of more than 70 million visits, the Chinese government quietly told government agencies and other work units to send groups, so the numbers would reach 70 million. Chinese people’s lack of manners, I really, really experienced it at the Expo: cutting in line, fighting over seats and so on~ Damn, what an embarrassment to the Chinese people. But, well, there weren’t many foreigners at the Meat Expo. It was mostly Chinese people, family, so no harm done……

A tragic country. A tragedy, a huge tragedy. Manners are something Chinese people absolutely have to improve. A great big country, with one ill-mannered person stacked on top of another, piling up one by one. To put it bluntly, it really is a tragedy. This country is divided into the “mainland” and the so-called Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. It’s a, holy crap~, a damn country of castes and ranks.

The day before yesterday a friend told me a story. He was eating at a restaurant in Paris, quietly enjoying his meal, when suddenly a big group of Chinese tourists showed up, and the quiet restaurant filled with the racket of drinking games. The waiter came over and asked him: “Are you people from Hong Kong?” My friend was mortified, because he knew what the waiter meant: mainlanders have no manners and don’t care about public decency, while people from Hong Kong are well-mannered……

Maybe this is exactly why China is split into the mainland, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan: those with manners and those without. Socialism is so advanced? That’s socialism with Chinese characteristics for you!

A tragic country, and we live inside the tragedy!

End of rant. Here are a few photos!

The USA Pavilion, love it:

The North Korea Pavilion, very good, very powerful:

The Israel Pavilion, too crowded, didn’t go in:


Very hard for ordinary people to get into:

This Expo was a real failure. The length of the lines killed all the fun.

The theme of this Expo seems better suited to people in urban planning!

title: The SweetTitles Plugin: Beautiful Title Tooltips
content:
The name Sweet Titles comes from a JS plugin that changes how title tooltips look: Sweet Titles Finalized.This plugin not only makes your title tooltips look nicer, it also shows the URL of the link you’re about to click, so users know where they’re going, which improves the user experience. Also, in my opinion, the system’s built-in title tooltips have a delay, while ones done in JS show up instantly. The plugin’s JS and CSS come from the guru leeiio, so first, thanks to him for his hard work. All I did was turn it into a plugin. Truly, one generation plants the trees and the next enjoys the shade! This is my very first work, so come check it out. If you’d rather not use a plugin, leeiio’s site has instructions for adding it by hand. OK, now let me introduce the plugin

  • Plugin name: sweetTitles (Chinese name: “Beautiful Titles”)
  • Initial version: 0.9
  • Release version: 1.4
  • Plugin conceived: August 5, 2010
  • Plugin released: August 19, 2010 (I was away traveling for part of that time, so I didn’t think about it for a long while)
  • What it does (screenshot): hover the mouse over a hyperlink and a floating tooltip for the link appears

About the plugin: it makes life easy for the lazy folks, who can get this effect without lifting a finger. But it has a downside too: it may cause jQuery to be loaded twice. Since this is the initial version, there are no admin options yet; those will come later. Future plans: I’ll add several options for users to choose from, letting you pick how jQuery is loaded, and you’ll be able to set sweetTitles’ CSS styles from the admin panel. I’ll also optimize the code and so on, so you get a better experience. Known issue: when using Windows Live Writer (the WLW offline editor), you may get an error that xmlrpc.php can’t be reached. After testing, it turns out this is caused by script support not being turned on. In the Windows Live Writer toolbar, go to Blog - Edit blog settings - Advanced - Blog overrides - Scripts, and choose to support them. That fixes the problem.

Thanks to everyone who helped me: leeiio (provided the JS and more), ilover (helped me revise the initial version, though in the end I rewrote it), hey33 (bravely tested the plugin for me), and Mumu. I’m really grateful for their selfless help. Thank you all! Official download: sweetTitles 1.4v

title: Tencent, Trying to Tie All Its Products Together
content:
People say Tencent is a bunch of bastards, but I don’t see it that way. All Tencent is doing is tying its own products together, and that’s actually a good thing. If you’d played every product and every game from every company out there, wouldn’t you have to remember the ID for each one, the password for each ID, and the security questions for each ID? That’s the benefit of bringing products together.

I don’t want to say too much about Tencent. Personally I think it’s way too flashy. Some things should be left for users to choose, not forced on them through hard selling and bundled installs. Hogging users’ desktops and grabbing market share by force is wrong~

Tencent is a double-edged sword: it can stab you, and it can also give you a hand up.

Last night we talked about QQ membership. I’ve been a QQ member for two years now, and QQ itself has only been around for 10 years. title: The Comic "The Darkess Outside Night": Did Anyone Get It?
content:
To be honest, when I first got the book and flipped through it, I just couldn’t make sense of the comic The Darkess Outside Night.

Later, meaning today, I woke up, grabbed the book from beside the bed, flipped through it again, and carefully studied every drawing in Chorus (Han Han’s magazine). Finally, when I got to the comic at the end, The Darkess Outside Night, I read it through once and at last I understood.

The meaning is actually simple. It seems to be a little sprite trapped in a bottle. To break out of the bottle and feel the sunlight outside, it slams into the wall of the bottle again and again, until finally, with one last violent crash, it dies with blood splattered everywhere. The bottle, lying next to a pile of garbage, shakes twice, and then everything goes still…

Very simple~ very human imagery~

Little people often reveal big truths. Don’t give up, don’t lose heart, fight with everything you have, and even if it leaves you bloody and broken, charge forward anyway. Just like the words “My Struggle” in the last panel of this comic. It isn’t only his struggle. All of us should have this kind of fighting spirit!

The original is in color. Below is the scanned version going around online.

Han Han’s Chorus is pretty good~ If you’re interested, please support Han Han by buying his book~

Disclaimer: I’m a Han Han fan and I support legit copies. I bought my own copy. The scanned version above has nothing to do with me.

title: Chapter 5: A China That Keeps Changing Flavor, and a Life That Only Recently Did
content: Today is Christmas, and yesterday was Christmas Eve, or maybe today is Christmas Eve (I mean on American time). Tonight I went out with my parents to a party for my dad’s work. I had no choice but to go. Eating, talking about work, what the hell does any of that have to do with me? And they made me go, when it was that cold outside. I didn’t want to a hundred times over, a thousand times over, but I had to go… I drank two bottles of beer. What a load of crap. That’s how it went. I remember that last year on December 24 I stayed home and didn’t go anywhere. The year before that, on December 24, there was a party at the branch office where my dad used to work. This year, because he was transferred, it was a party for the regional branch. The place is the same, but the people have changed… China keeps changing flavor, and it keeps giving me this feeling: “The General Administration of Press and Publication recently issued a notice calling for further standardization of language in publications. The notice requires that Chinese-language publications must not casually mix in English words, letter abbreviations or other foreign words; must not coin words that are neither Chinese nor foreign and whose meaning is unclear; and must not arbitrarily add or remove letters from foreign words, reverse word order, or otherwise violate language norms.” It makes some sense, but it’s still a bullshit move. As for my life, which only recently changed flavor, I don’t know whether that flavor is sweet or bitter. I can’t taste it anymore. I know it’s changed, but I don’t know what it tastes like…

title: About the GPL
content:
My old WhiteLove theme is licensed under the GPL. So what is the GPL? Put simply, you can remove the author’s name, but you must keep the code open source. Users are allowed to modify it however they like, but you have to follow the corresponding terms. The main principles of the GPL:

  1. It ensures the software is always released as open source from start to finish, protecting the work from being stolen and sold commercially. Any piece of software that uses the source code of third-party software protected by the GPL, and is distributed to people outside the development team, automatically becomes an entity protected and bound by the GPL itself. In other words, at that point it must open its source code.
  2. The GPL is essentially an expression of copyleft (also translated as “anti-copyright,” “copyright left,” “all rights reversed,” and so on). You can remove all of the original work’s copyright information, as long as you keep it open source and include the GPL license with the source code and binaries, so that those who come after can clearly see how the software is licensed. The essence of the GPL is that, as long as the software stays fully open source, users get as much room as possible to do what they want with it, so the software develops faster and better.
  3. No matter how the software is distributed, the source code must be included. For example, if it’s offered for download on the web, a link to download the source code must be clearly provided on the same page as the binary download (if there is one). If it’s distributed on disc, a disc with the source files must be included.
  4. Companies or individuals who develop or maintain software under the GPL may charge users a certain service fee. But the same old rule applies: the complete source code of the software must be provided free of charge, and the source code may not be bundled with services or sold in any disguised bundle. This doesn’t apply to themes that don’t declare that they follow the GPL. Of course, all my work follows this license. WhiteLove and the Vivian theme I’m using now were both modified from existing theme frameworks.

Wikipedia says:

Rights granted: The terms and conditions of the GPL apply to anyone who receives a work under the GPL (the “licensee”). Any licensee who accepts these terms and conditions is granted permission to modify, copy and redistribute the work or derivative versions of it. The licensee may charge a fee for this service, or not. This is the biggest difference between the GPL and other free software licenses that prohibit commercial use. Stallman believes free software should not restrict commercial use, and the GPL states this clearly. But the GPL also stipulates that distributors may not restrict the rights the GPL grants. For example, this prohibits distributing the software under a shrink-wrap (passive, implied) license or contract. Distributors under the GPL also agree that patents used in the software may be used in other GPL software. Copyleft: The GPL does not grant licensees unlimited rights. The right to redistribute is granted only if the licensee makes the software’s source code, and all modifications, available. Copies and modified versions must also be licensed under the GPL. These requirements are what copyleft is, and it rests on the fact that the work is copyrighted. Because it is copyrighted, the licensee has no right to modify or redistribute it (except under fair use) unless there is a copyleft clause. Anyone who wants to exercise rights normally prohibited by law only needs to agree to the terms of the GPL. Conversely, if someone distributes software in violation of the GPL (for example, by not releasing the source code), they may be sued by the original author. Copyleft uses copyright law to achieve the opposite of its purpose: copyleft gives people inalienable rights rather than the many restrictions imposed by copyright law. This is why the GPL is called “hacked copyright law.” Many distributors of GPL software bundle the source code with the executables. Another approach is to provide the source code on physical media (such as a CD). In practice, a lot of GPL software is distributed over the internet, and much of the source code is also available via FTP. Copyleft only takes effect when a program is redistributed. Modifications to the software don’t have to be made public or open source, as long as they aren’t distributed. Note that copyleft applies only to the software, not to the software’s output (unless the output is the software itself). This may change in version 3 of the GPL, however. The GPL is a license: The GPL is designed as a license, not a contract. In common-law countries there is a clear legal distinction between a license and a contract: a contract is enforced by contract law, while the GPL, as a license, is enforced by copyright law. In many civil-law countries, however, there is no such distinction. The principle of the GPL is simple: under copyright law, if you don’t follow the GPL’s terms and conditions, you don’t have the corresponding rights. And without the GPL, copyright law applies to the work by default; the work does not enter the public domain.

For details, see GNU General Public License

title: Wait, the Short Film We're About to Shoot
content: College life is full of unknowns. From morning to night I’m always busy, yet I couldn’t tell you what I’m busy with. Today I met the female lead of the short film. I’m the male lead, but the female lead… how do I put it, she’s pretty short, and I have no idea how the director picked her. Oh well, I already said yes, so I’ll just grit my teeth and do it. What’s happened lately has made me feel that the only person I can really count on is myself. Everyone else is fake; only I and my family are truly worth trusting, and the ones who let you down the moment it matters are your friends. I thought the short film we’re about to shoot was just a graduation project for an upperclassman a year ahead of me, something shot for fun. Only after I took it on did I find out it’s an entry for a competition. Well, only then did it sink in. But I hadn’t been treating it carelessly before either. I take everything seriously, especially things I’ve promised other people. Lately I’ve liked jotting down sudden flashes of inspiration in my phone’s notes app, and there are two lines I want to keep reminding myself of: Learn to endure loneliness; life calls for keeping a low profile. You can’t borrow money or ask for money your whole life; one day you’ll have to pay it back. That second line makes me sad no matter what. I’ve spent all my living allowance. My parents didn’t give me enough and told me to ask them for more, but I just can’t bring myself to ask. Honestly, I don’t want to spend my family’s money anymore, but I don’t have a job right now, so there’s nothing I can do. One of our teachers once said that even if your family doesn’t give you money, you can still live just fine, because every person, every animal, has the will to survive. You can stay alive; you can find a job and live perfectly well. I want to give it a try. I’ll record every bit of my life here, without leaving anything out. Starting today I’m going to spend a lot more time at the library and let myself soak in the ocean of knowledge. Just wait for it: Wait.

title: On the Gaokao, and On My Last Few Days
content:
The gaokao, the national college entrance exam, is happening right now, and we have a few days off. A lot of my classmates have quieted down to follow it. We’re all in our second year of high school, so naturally we care about the gaokao, that so-called turning point in life.

I don’t know why, but I get nervous sometimes too. On the day of the exam I felt strangely nervous, which I never expected. The gaokao: in elementary school I didn’t care about it; in middle school I just listened to my parents nag about the high school entrance exam; and now in high school, the gaokao is finally coming. The nerves brought on a few thoughts.

Two-thirds of high school is already behind me. Two of my three years just slipped away like that? Every day it’s always

home — on the bus — school — on the bus — school — on the bus — home

that kind of life. School days have every flavor: sweet, sour, bitter, spicy, you name it. The fun days always fly by, and the boring ones fly by too. What have I learned in two years of high school? No idea~ It feels like I’ve been in a slump the whole time…… on and on with no end……

From the summer before my second year until now, I just haven’t gotten into gear. Things have only gotten a bit better lately~

Every day I daydream about when I’ll go abroad, but…… for now I’m climbing up step by step! It’s exhausting and hard, but it’s worth it!

Today the seniors finished their exams, and it rained here today too! Heaven is crying! China’s imperial examination system still shapes all of this. That’s how it was 1,000 years ago, and that’s how it will be 1,000 years from now!

I recommend everyone watch the video “Harmony Saves the Crisis.” What that eminent monk says is absolutely right, but will the ruling party actually do it? No, they have their own interests to look after~ heh. Don’t dream of changing society, and don’t try to take on the government. We can’t beat them.

Back to the gaokao: right after it ended today, people were already setting off firecrackers~ What a joke~ What are the firecrackers for~ So pointless~

Now let me talk about me these last few days~

These past few days I’ve been staying home, reading and working on my website. I moved the site from Xirang, a Chinese host, to one abroad, from the Celestial Empire to the good old USA, and now everything’s OK! I’ve got hosting, a domain, a theme, ads, everything! Haha~ so happy~ hehe~

This morning I went to the hospital and finally got the braces I’d worn for over a year taken off, and then they put a retainer on me. Sigh~ The tragic part is I have to wear the retainer for another year, and for the first six months it’s 24 hours a day. Only in the second half can I skip it during the day and just wear it at night. Right now it makes me slur my words. How am I going to get through the days ahead~ uh~ I can’t even imagine~

The academic proficiency test is coming up soon, and I’m a bit nervous. If I do well, going abroad will be a real possibility. Bless me, my lord, my god!

OK, I’m done rambling~ that’s about it~

Byebye everyone~

title: The Phoniness of Huainan No. 1 High School
content:
I’ve been in high school for two years now. Over these two years I’ve kept growing, figuring some things out, and getting a taste of some things.

Today was another so-called show day, a day of putting on a show that made life hard for us. Putting on a show, that’s no exaggeration. The so-called Open Teaching Day is all fake. On this day we wear school uniforms. On this day no messing around is allowed. On this day we have to be polite. On this day we have to listen carefully in class. On this day classes can’t go over practice problems, only new lessons. On this day you can’t be late, and if you’re late you’re done for. Everything on this day is the opposite of normal. The day goes by both fast and slow. All of it fake, and tomorrow everything goes back to the way it was!

Our vice principal’s face, really, it’s the face of someone who sucks up to his superiors and looks down on those below him. I guess all Chinese officials have that face~ Sleazy & filthy!

Let’s leave our principals a little dignity~ Principals, because our high school has four of them, one principal and three vice principals, and the actual principal is never at school. Most of the time he just has his name on the title~

As for so-and-so, the teachers are good people, good by nature, but after being egged on by the so-called leaders, they start getting into “illegal business,” drilling communist ideology into us. Heh~ what a tragedy~

Let me talk about our vice principal some more. What I remember most is him sucking up to one of our alumni who had retired, a former vice governor of Shanxi Province, when he came back to visit the school. When the old man was about to speak, our vice principal said, “Let us invite XX to deliver an important speech.” Then the old man got up and said, “First let me say this isn’t an important speech, I’m just sharing a few thoughts…” Heh~ Right then I thought the vice principal was disgusting. So used to licking his superiors’ asses, huh? This time nobody wanted him to, and, heh, awkward, right? So fucking disgusting~

Open Teaching Day~ that’s China’s formalism for you, heh~ You know, it’d be great if they charged admission for Open Teaching Day. That would boost revenue and boost motivation at the same time~

Why teach just for the sake of Open Teaching Day? Huainan No. 1 High School is despicable~ All surface work~ All formalism~ Is there hope for Chinese education? No~ I hope I’m right about that~

A bunch of principals plus a pile of teachers, what’s that? A pile of dung heaped up over there? I’ll stay away from them~ so they don’t pollute my mind~

Wen Song, the head of our junior-year group, heh~ acts like he’s such a big deal every day~ high and mighty, never letting go of anything we do wrong~ What a tragedy~ Wen Song, oh Wen Song, Huainan No. 1 High School’s “teacher” Wen Song, how can you be like this as a human being? You’re a tragedy of the human race~ A moment of silence for you~

All hollow and fake. No. 1 High can’t compare to No. 2 High~ But then schools can’t really be compared, because schools aren’t the same kind of entity to begin with~

We live in an environment where a hundred schools of thought contend. No. 1 High says our mindset is to get into a second-tier university, No. 2 High says our mindset is to get into a first-tier university, No. 3 High says our mindset is to get into a third-tier university, and No. 24 High says we’re just here to have fun~ pass through and say we went to high school~ Heh~ just joking~ don’t take it to heart~

The hypocrisy, phoniness and hollowness of Huainan No. 1 High School can’t be described in words. You have to experience it all yourself. All of it disgusts me, so I’ll stop writing~

Finally

Today I’m ashamed of Huainan No. 1 High School; tomorrow Huainan No. 1 High School will be proud of me!

That’s my guiding principle!

title: Late Autumn
content:
It’s been a long time since I sat at a keyboard for my blog, a long time since I wrote any kind of Chinese blog post. Just like that, half a year went by in a blink, and more than a year in the US went by too. Last month I switched the blog’s engine from jeklly to hexo, back to nodejs, which I used to know well. Over this year technology has changed at a dizzying pace, so fast that keeping up has left me a bit tired and helpless.

I know it’s already winter back in China, and it’s started snowing in my hometown, but here I can still wear a T-shirt, so let’s call it late autumn.

Coming to the US gave me a fresh understanding of learning. These days I like organizing things more and more: organizing notes, organizing files, organizing key points. Maybe that’s the American way of thinking: out of a jumbled mess, pick out the few items you need and line them up neatly, ready for when you need them.

They say what goes around comes around

Yes, they’re right. I spent a few carefree years in high school, didn’t care when I bombed the gaokao, and went to a junior college. But what I’m facing now is a university that I think is even harder to handle than the gaokao. A friend says as long as I put my heart into it I’ll be fine. Sure, but putting my heart into it is exhausting.

In the past four months I’ve splurged on a lot of stuff. In order of purchase: first a NAS, a Synology DS415Play, a UPS backup power supply, an R7000 router, a DELL U2415 monitor, an HHKB Type-S, a Magic Trackpad, a Bother scanner-printer, a New 3DS XL… plus some other handy software…

title: Who Understands My Pain? My Silence, My Own Loneliness
content:
A long time ago I said I was sick of this society. A long time ago I said I liked someone. A long time ago I went after someone with actual actions. A long time ago… that’s all in the past. I feel like I should bring it up, or maybe there’s no need to anymore… Who understands my pain? I bear my pain myself. No need to tell other people. I carry my pain on my own; sharing it with others, it’s still pain. In the end all I can do is cry by myself, cry inside. My own pain is mine to work through. My silence doesn’t mean I agree with you. My silence doesn’t mean I oppose you. My silence doesn’t mean I’ve given up. My silence, you can treat it as a fart… Who understands my pain? Who can know who is whose pain? Who can see who is hurting? Mystery! Shit! I admit I live in my own world, enjoying things alone, being happy alone, alone… No! I’m not alone. Oh! I’ve got a bunch of buddies. The tragic part is there are hardly any girls… I haven’t been happy for a year… I haven’t known what being truly happy feels like for a long time. What is real happiness? I’m so repressed. My worries, my unhappiness… I really need to go see a therapist. I don’t know why. What on earth could make me happy? My pain, where exactly does it hurt? The happy things… are gone. I know there’s a wound in my heart, but I don’t know how to mend it… Really, it hurts so much. Save me? Can you help me? When will days like this end? I don’t know. I stay holed up at home for a whole week at a time. I went to Shanghai once and wasn’t happy at all; it just left me with more regrets. I don’t know what to say… All I know is that I missed my time and my chance. It’s gone, really gone, everything’s gone… This isn’t a piece of literature, just how I really feel. My wound throbs. When will a wound of the heart heal? I haven’t laughed from the heart in a year… who can feel this? The pressure is too much… a whole year, and not one thing has made me truly laugh, made me happy. Nothing… repressed… so repressed… Where is my future headed… why is that all I think about every day… Still, the smile I usually wear isn’t fake, it isn’t a polite smile, it’s just a goofy grin… Is there anything I can look back on and relish talking about? No… I always think about my failures. I’ve failed so many times. Since ninth grade… I haven’t succeeded at anything… In high school a lot of what I did wasn’t recognized, and a lot of things only got solved by talking people around. I’m so tired… so tired… My pain, you don’t understand: silence and loneliness

PS: TOEFL on the 21st, not counting on it. No idea how things will go when school starts…

title: My 2014
content:
Time slips by so fast that I can’t catch hold of either end of it. By the time I come back to my senses, it’s gone. Looking back on my 2014, it just feels like it vanished in a rush.

My 2014 was split in two: one part in China, one part in the US.

Looking back on 2014, I went to Bengbu, Hefei, Rizhao, Hangzhou, Shanghai, Los Angeles, Phoenix and Tucson.

(A Flash video used to be here. It can no longer be played.)

“Nanshan Nan” was my favorite song at the end of 2014.

Let me look back on the part in China.

00

I remember that after school started last February, I stayed in Bengbu for only about a week before going to Hefei for a training program at a company. Checking my photo album, I went to Hefei on February 25.

The school bus took all of us to Hefei together. Pangzi was sitting next to me, and Xiaohei and Wu Guoguo were behind us,

On March 28, my girlfriend and I set off for Shanghai to see Yayoi Kusama’s art exhibition, and we went back on March 30.

The mirror room

After I got back, in April I got a buzz cut in Hefei, only two millimeters long. It felt nice and cool.

In May, on the 17th, I went to another concert in Hefei. Every time I go to the Hefei Olympic Sports Center, I take a picture of you in the same spot.

June. I still remember that on May 30, the day vacation had just started, I saw the SegmentFault event and couldn’t sleep all night. I told myself that if I didn’t go for it now, it would be too late. So the next day I bought a high-speed rail ticket, stood for several hours, and arrived in Hangzhou for the competition. It was my first time staying in a youth hostel, just because it was cheap and saved some money.

This is early in the morning on June 1, before heading out from the youth hostel

A group photo of everyone there, SegmentFault’s second anniversary

The team I formed on site. The good friends I made at this competition were the biggest takeaway

At that competition I also met an online friend I’d never met in person, who is also a good friend I hadn’t seen in years

In the end we won a grand prize. Thanks to Xiaocao and Lyojo for pulling an all-nighter with me. I also remember taking a hard-seat train back from Hangzhou all by myself. Going home alone, I almost fell asleep in the waiting hall, and once on the train I slept the whole night. It was just a seat, but I was so tired, and when I woke up I was right at home. Then around June 7 I went to Rizhao and had fun for two whole days. It was great. We had barbecue and Korean cold noodles.

After that the training program ended and I got ready to leave Hefei. I remember that at the end of June I got my offer from UA and got ready to set off for the US.

These are the roommates I was closest to in college. One of them wasn’t there, so it was just the four of us, and we took our last group photo of 2014 together. Back then we complained about this and that, and only after leaving did I realize that was the best time. I never had a complete high school experience, and now I don’t have a complete college experience either. After only two years together, my college life in China was over.

01

This section is my summer vacation. I don’t know if it counts as my last summer vacation in China. The whole vacation was only a month long. During that month I went to Shanghai for my visa interview, then took driving lessons and passed the second part of the driving test, only to realize that I’d basically wasted the whole summer.

On August 11, I set off for Shanghai, with my parents along. After eating my last meal in China in 2014 at the Ajisen Ramen at Pudong Airport, I walked through the departure checkpoint without looking back. My dad told me my mom cried that day after I left. At the time I wasn’t sad at all, probably too excited. It was only after arriving in the US that I slowly started to get homesick.

The Boeing 787

This is that night, flying to Tucson, over LA

10

In Tucson I met a bunch of buddies who give me a hard time but also really look out for me. We all have a great time together. I’m pretty happy with how things are now.

My school, UA

Actually, during my time in the US, going from bursting with novelty to now being homesick, missing the food from home, there’s a feeling I really can’t put into words. It’s bottled up in my heart and won’t go away. I remember it was about a month after I came to the US. One night I was making pig’s trotter soup at home, and while I was making it I thought of how my mom used to make me pig’s trotter soup every time I came home from out of town. I couldn’t stop the tears, and I cried the whole night. I’ve also regretted it, asking myself why I came here, but in the end I still told myself: it was my dream, and even if I have to crawl, I’ll crawl all the way to the end.

Coming to the US brought a lot of firsts: the first time cutting my own hair, the first time bowling, the first time cooking for someone else, the first time moving…

Of course, I guess only by going through all this do you really grow up.

So much happened this year. Sometimes I feel the year went by too slowly, making me live through so much turmoil. Sometimes I feel it went by too fast, ending before I could really savor the life in it. Maybe that’s just life. My 2014, goodbye, I’ll never see you again. Maybe I’ll be grateful to this year for making me a lot more mature and helping me grow up quite a bit.

Finally

Maybe you’ll ask me how I’m doing now. I’ll tell you “good,” but the real pain is something only I know. Treat happiness as life, and treat troubles as seasoning. Only by fighting your way through life do you become mature and steady. Hello, 2015, here I come.

title: A College Life to Mourn, and a Choice
content:
I’m watching my college career come to an end before it even really began. Whatever else I can say, I’ve gained a lot in these two years. Right now I’m in Hefei, doing a training program at iFlytek Education.

Waiting

This is the second half of my sophomore year. I came to Hefei disappointed and feeling lost. Deep down I didn’t want to come here, but I had no choice. Everything here is just awful. Apart from the food and housing being a bit better, everything else is basically the same as before.

Choice

My classmates around me are all playing LOL or other games. I rarely play games myself, and I rarely ask them why they love playing so much. For them, maybe games really are the only place they can find any fun. They haven’t grown up inside. Maybe it’s just a different worldview, or maybe that’s why they ended up here. Like frogs at the bottom of a well, they only look at the patch of sky above them and have no wish to climb any higher.

Hope

I’ve decided to take my own road. I hope I can succeed and keep going.

title: A Frustrating Afternoon
content: This morning I got up pretty early for me, at 9:30, because I went to bed early last night. Then I rushed off to the exit-entry hall at the Public Security Bureau to apply for a passport.Sigh, getting a passport this early, I really had no choice. My school doesn’t give me a student ID, so the only way to take the TOEFL is with a passport. Sad, just sad. Still, it’s good to get it done early, it’ll make things a little easier later… In the afternoon, well, more like around noon, things got even more frustrating. This site got hijacked and redirected for no reason to 61.132.255.212. Ha, this is Anhui Telecom’s handiwork. It was hijacked for a full 5 hours and I couldn’t log in. Ha. Then I bothered customer support and asked what was going on, and the answer was that it loaded fine on their end. Well, uh~~~ Telecom really is brilliant! Here are some ways to deal with this situation: Method 1: Edit your computer’s routing table. Note: the routing table, not the hosts file, because Telecom’s ad injection no longer relies only on DNS hijacking. The command to permanently change the routing table on Windows: “Accessories” - “cmd”, which needs to be run as administrator. Then enter the following route -p add 61.132.255.212 mask 255.255.255.255 127.0.0.1 route -p add 61.132.221.146 mask 255.255.255.255 127.0.0.1 Method 2: Edit the routing table on your ADSL modem. I recommend this one. You do it once and you’re done, and it’s especially good if more than one computer in your home goes online. The Telecom-provided ADSL modem at my house is a fairly old model. For how to log in to the ADSL modem, see one of my earlier posts. Click “Advanced Settings” –> “Routing Settings” –> “Static Routes” in order, then in the main window on the right, click the “Add” button to add a route. IP address: the IP you want to block, e.g. 61.132.255.212 Subnet mask: 255.255.255.255 Gateway IP address: 127.0.0.1 Be sure to save once you’ve edited the routing table, and the settings only take effect after you restart the ADSL modem! The methods are partly reposted from the blog of Zhuzaixiao

title: How to Set Up Wildcard Domains in DirectAdmin
content:
This was something from a month ago. I installed WordPress on a DirectAdmin panel and turned on Multisite. Since DirectAdmin doesn’t support adding * subdomains, you have to edit the config file by hand, which is what this post is about. To set it up for a single domain, first log in over SSH (you need root) and enter the following commands, replacing yourdomain.com with your own domain

Find ServerAlias www.yourdomain.com yourdomain.com

Add this after it: *.yourdomain.com

So it becomes ServerAlias www.yourdomain.com yourdomain.com *.yourdomain.com

Save, restart Apache, and your wildcard record takes effect. PS: I’ve noticed I’m getting used to writing posts in HTML…… the visual editor is garbage……

title: Dreaming of Chasing a Dream: What Are We Thinking? In a Dream
content:
I live in my dream. I’m Chinese, proudly and openly Chinese. I’m not ashamed of being Chinese, and I’m not embarrassed to be Chinese! The Chinese people, the nation, and I mean the nation as a people, not the so-called PRC. Still, I’m proud of the PRC too! China’s strength couldn’t have happened without the GOV. From the middle of the twentieth century until now, honestly, from my china history textbook I’ve felt how strong China has become~ and I really admire it. That’s not sarcasm, it’s praise!

Today I got my passport. It’s for the TOEFL, or let’s say it’ll come in handy later. In class today I did some careful math. The time is close. I’m planning to take it twice, in June and in July. Roughly speaking, that leaves 3 months and 4 months. It’s not early anymore, and I don’t want to end up accomplishing nothing.

In a recent weekly journal, well, not that recent actually, it was the one from winter break, I wrote an essay titled “What Are We Thinking?” What are we thinking? I asked and answered it myself: “I know what I’m thinking. What are we thinking? We don’t know!”

Ask yourself, right now, ask yourself: “What am I thinking?” Filling my stomach, making money, getting a girlfriend, getting married, having kids… the path society lays out. That’s what we think about, right~

Why am I writing this? I’m not really sure. It’s just that one day I suddenly remembered my own dream. Will everyone one day suddenly remember their dream and then actually do something about it?

Our lives are trapped inside a tiny circle around us. We can’t get out, but others can get in. So our dreams slowly die inside the circle, and then our children and grandchildren grow conceited and arrogant~ like the frog at the bottom of the well.

Economy or education, which matters more? I can’t figure out which one matters more, so I’ll let you all take a guess~

I once wrote a short essay called “Education Is the Foundation of a Nation,” and later I threw it away like trash. It’s true, in the PRC you don’t talk about this kind of thing, and I don’t plan to say much more. In the past I wrote lots and lots of things down on paper and then forgot them. I think that’s the most realistic reality, the best way to forget your complaints and not get upset over things. At least on paper nothing gets “harmonized,” and there’s no filter checking for banned words~~ heh

Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou… these cities don’t represent China. China is one whole. Only when we can talk about a tiny village being developed will that be the real China!

What are we thinking? Many people have forgotten that they’re a kind of animal. Many people have forgotten what time is. Many people have forgotten the essence of life. Many people have forgotten where we came from. Many people have forgotten their childhood dreams. So they live just to stay alive, live for money, and some live for power, to protect and hold on to their own power…

What are we thinking? Why do we think this way? Our few decades of industrialization equal a few hundred years of capitalism, yet our thinking has progressed even more slowly than thinking did during capitalist industrialization. People call it the “Celestial Empire,” and that’s an undeniable fact.

Strong on the outside, weak on the inside. That’s how Chinese people abroad are well protected by their country, while at home………..

What are we thinking? I have no way of knowing, and it seems I don’t want to know anymore. 1.3 billion people. I’d like to think 80% of them know what they’re thinking. They should. Chinese people understand very well what they’re thinking. 80% is what I hope for. Maybe it’s not that many, maybe it’s more, but none of that seems to be any of my business. So why do I make a guess? Because I’m Chinese!

I’m in no position to say all this. I realize I’m not a celebrity… not a good student… not an official… no money… no power… no connections… no…

I’m just an ordinary person

A true descendant of the Chinese people!

Right now I only live in my dream, because I’m still some distance from my reality. It seems far away, but if I keep moving forward, I can succeed~ I haven’t forgotten the vow I made with my friends: see you at UC Berkeley~

What I used to pursue, I understand now, was all a dream I can’t make happen. I know that once politics gets involved, everything seems to………..

Silence… my choice…

Some recent news, while I’m at it:

I recently switched hosting to “Xirang,” and I think it’s pretty good. About 5V55, I really have to say: “@#￥%&……*……￥$#@^^^…… (several hundred words of profanity omitted).” The speed difference between the two hosts is huge. The new one is really fast, super fast~ and there are none of the script errors I used to get. Those script errors really did a number on me~ and now that’s finally solved~

My domain is probably still in 5V55’s hands~ even though I’m the one who registered it, heh

I’m planning to transfer it to Go Daddy at the end of April. I can’t stay in China, heh. That’s going to cost me some more money again~

I don’t know if I can get the domain transfer code~ All I can say is, I hope nothing goes wrong~

Since my domain is in 5V55’s “hands,” I won’t post too many opinions. I’ll keep a low profile~~~~~~!

Today is March 18, 2010

“Keep living my dream!”

Said the me who’s still dreaming. Go for it~

Keep moving forward, even through tears~

There’s nothing painful about it

The joy at the finish line is waiting for you~

Think differently from others

Act differently from others

That’s how you can bring change~

content: The end.

title: Grinning Through Life's Hard Times
content: Tears welling up in my eyes, I sneezed, smiled, and laughed it off.

title: A Cool Breeze. Is It Fall Again?
content: It’s been about half a year since I last came here. Is a blog that hasn’t been updated in ages still a blog? Listening to music and tapping out these words, I wonder what you, on the other side of the screen, are doing right now. Over this half year, this past year or so, my moods have swung a lot. I’ve gone from aiming too high to keeping my feet on the ground, and I want to take things one step at a time and rewrite the road ahead of me. There’s so much I want to say, but when it gets to the tip of my tongue I don’t know where to begin. This year I scored just over 200 on the gaokao, and through what Chinese people call “connections” I got into a junior college. I suppose it still counts as college: a year and a half in Bengbu, a year and a half in Hefei, and at the end I can still go on to an adult-education bachelor’s degree. I have to work hard on the road ahead. I chose Software Technology (Computer Programming and Applications) as my major, and thinking it over, I don’t regret it. I love this stuff. I spent the whole summer break working, and I’ve grown up a lot. Keep a low profile, stay steady: those few words really are the foundation for standing on your own in this society. Don’t draw attention to yourself, and don’t stick your nose into other people’s business. A reminder to my future self: I hope from now on I study with my feet on the ground and stop daydreaming. And to all you blog friends I’ve neglected: hello. PS: I removed more than half of my blogroll and am starting to update the blog regularly. My real blogging life begins now.

title: Back to School
content: After school started, instead of classes we began a practical training program, developing a Java project in small teams. I’m team lead again, and I’m going to be teaching people again too. It feels pretty good. I’ve felt a lot this past year; after all, I mean to keep this blog as a diary. With all the code I’ve written along the way, I wonder if it would wrap around the Earth. I hope I keep growing every day. I passed the English Level B exam with an 82, and I need to keep working at it. I know what I want to do, and I’m lucky.

title: A Cheerful Afternoon
content:
Yesterday I kept a low profile and stayed holed up at home. Today I went out for a stroll~~

This afternoon I went out for a bit. Yesterday I stayed home all day and spent less time online. I think I spent the whole day seriously listening to English, and then in the evening I went online for a little while, which seems to have lasted until 3 this morning, heh

Today is Sunday. We live in a residential area right next to the shopping district, so it’s kind of noisy. I hate this kind of environment, but I also seem to depend on it to get by.

I went past my old middle school, which I hadn’t been to in a long time. I was just passing by. The school has changed a lot. It’s been more than a year since I left middle school, and I miss it but can’t go back. Everyone misses the old days and thinks back on the past, but we always have to keep moving forward, look ahead, and stop clinging to the past.

The afternoon sun was lovely, without the glare of summer or the clash of winter and its cold wind. It was so comfortable it made you sleepy. People on the street were out shopping, and I was just passing through, hurrying home from a friend’s place.

This afternoon I saw a friend from middle school. He goes to school in another city, so I usually only get to see him during the holidays. This buddy of mine is pretty chubby, haha~

On the way I wandered a bit to see if there was anything tasty I could get Mom to buy~~o(∩_∩)o

The money I had on me (my New Year’s red envelope money) has run dry because of the website

So on March 16 I started my savings plan

Today is March 16. The plan is to save up 300 yuan by the end of June. Sticking to the principle of thrift and no waste, I’ll save up the full 300 yuan to register a domain with godaddy, move my domain out of China and go international, plus a haircut card

Ask Dad for 100 yuan for the haircut card

I have 40 yuan on hand, and I’ll ask Grandpa for 20

60 yuan

60 + Zhu Kemao’s 90 yuan

The 90 yuan has to be paid back within 3 weeks

Ding Ke can chip in 50, I guess~

Then I only need to pay Zhu Kemao back 40 yuan

I still need to save 300-90-60=150 yuan myself

Actually that number is more than enough

150 yuan

Saved up in 3 weeks

50 a week

so easy~

Monday, ask Mom for 10 yuan

Tuesday, ask Dad for 10 yuan

Thursday, ask Mom for 10 yuan

Um

It really is a bit hard

Work hard

Go for it~~

This plan is a bit shameless, but I’ve posted it here with nothing held back. I hope it gives you some ideas, (^__^)

Feeling the warmth of the sun, I forgot some of my worries for a while

So

My mood this afternoon was really cheerful

Heh

It really is March’s peach-blossom snow and April’s lovely mood~~

title: What Kind of Firmware Is This, Teclast? You've Got to Be Kidding Me~
content:
The day before yesterday I happened to wonder whether there was a firmware update for my MP4 player, so I went to Teclast’s official site to check, and sure enough there was one, from September this year. Mine is a Teclast TL-C300-VE (bought in ‘09; the one before it was an Aigo. Why did I switch to Teclast? There’s a little story behind that, see the PS below). The firmware it came with was version 5.0, and now 5.1 is out. So I downloaded it and planned to flash it tonight.

In the evening I opened the software, switched modes, loaded the firmware, started flashing, and everything seemed OK. Formatted the MP4, rebooted, and damn, the touch buttons stopped working. I couldn’t select anything… I figured I’d done something wrong, so I tried 10 times, and it still didn’t work. You’ve got to be kidding me! So I decided to flash it back to the original 5.0 firmware… but there was one big problem: where was I supposed to find 5.0? So I started Googling. Since 5.0 and 5.1 came out a year apart, and Teclast’s official site doesn’t keep old firmware versions, seriously, are you kidding me! I gritted my teeth and searched for over half an hour and finally found it, in some dark little corner of the internet. Then I went through the same steps and finally managed to flash it back… Teclast, you’re ripping us off… What kind of upgrade is this… it’s a downgrade! A heads-up for other TL-C300-VE users: just stick with the original 5.0 firmware. Do not flash 5.1… once you flash it the touch controls stop working. If you’ve already flashed it, flash it back… I’ve put the TL-C300VE-V5.03-C4C5 firmware package and tool up for download here: TL-C300VE-V5.03-C4C5 firmware and mass production tool PS: Teclast, you rip-off, when you update firmware could you please keep the old versions available? Sigh, I’m broke and can’t afford an iPod… so I’ll make do with Teclast… The one before was an Aigo. I remember I bought it on August 8, 2008, the day of the Olympics opening ceremony. One day in ‘09, a classmate asked me in the morning to download some dirty movies for him, and I said yes. In the afternoon I went to school on the bus, which was seriously packed. I got shoved around on the bus and ended up pressed against a handrail. I had put that Aigo MP4 in the outermost pocket of my backpack. At the time I just felt something crack, but it didn’t occur to me that it was the MP4. In afternoon class, I gave the MP4 to my classmate. “Huh? Why is the screen all messed up?” he asked, confused, and right then it hit me… it got crushed, and the screen was broken. So in September ‘09 I bought this one. I’ve noticed a lot of things don’t last a year in my hands… except my laptop, of course… Addendum: the night of January 6, 2011. I got up in the middle of the night to use the bathroom and snapped the power switch… Damn, I’m a real genius.

title: In a Chaotic World, I Focus on Living
content:
I’ve found I have a lot I want to write in my journal. I haven’t been to school in half a year, and a lot of things are stuck inside me. I have no friends in real life. It’s not that I don’t have friends, it’s that they’re all too busy. They’re all high school seniors. Born in China, what freedom is there to speak of? The gaokao has locked them up. So all I do every day is type, type, and type. Or read, or write and doodle…

Life is so beautiful. That’s the line I put in my QQ status in the early hours of the morning.

Every day I scroll through microblogs and read other people’s blogs, living a leisurely, carefree life, haha. A while ago I said I’d write a post about what I’ve learned from building websites, but I’m lazy so I never did. I’ll try to write it this year.

These past few days I’ve been reading the news, getting a sense of global trends, and reading posts from fellow bloggers. What I want to say is: in a chaotic world, I focus on living.

For a long time I’ve had this idea: save up some money and go live a pastoral life someday. There are all kinds of people in this world, and I know what kind of person I am. To live a carefree life, how nice would that be? Murky politics, why should we let them draw lines for us? Let them, the politicians, stir up the muddy water over there! Why care about them? People in capitalist societies care about politics for the sake of social welfare? Then why do we care about politics? For what? Great communism? Oh, I suppose so. In that case, I’ll just stay an independent with no party.

In a chaotic world, why should we complain? Does complaining only end in bloodshed? Let history decide.

Let them play their own games, and I’ll live my life. When war breaks out, it’s just death, right? Heh, no big deal. History gave me my life, and history can end it. I think that’s fair.

Life is beautiful, and living is beautiful too, so why complain? CCAV promotes the CCP, and what does CNN promote? XXX-CCP? Heh, I guess so. What a pair of pointless “people.”

Okay, enough of that.

One last thing: I just focus on my own life.

Next entry: “What is ShowBLOG?” Stay tuned.

10.07.2015 update

This ShowBLOG thing never got off the ground, because back then I didn’t know any tech at all, so I had to give up, and that was the end of this simple dream. Maybe one day I’ll get bored and try writing it, but it feels so pointless and silly.

title: Where the Blog Began: Chasing a Dream, Only to See It Shattered
content: This is a journal entry I’ll never finish, never ever finish, because human desire is endless. I think it can stand for what I think. I’m made up inside it, but in reality I exist. I’m writing this to myself: I won’t cry anymore. I’ll face everything with strength, give up on nothing, shed no more tears, and look at myself with a smile… The dream within a dream is the most real, because nobody bothers me there. While I’m awake, the me in the dream is still dreaming that dream. On street after street, people brush past me. After the rain, filthy muddy water splashes everywhere. I know there’s nothing I can do about it, so all I can do is dodge it and face the street, a thing that has nothing to do with me. Taxis park wherever they like. As long as you have connections, ha, everything is easy. That’s society. It’s heartless, and yet it has its own goddamn kind of heart. Chinese people, people, are all like this. I walk on. Why should I try to understand people who have nothing to do with me? People should live a life that’s worth something. I think I’d make a pretty good public speaker. Being a legal pyramid-scheme salesman is what I consider the ideal job. Or maybe I’ll be a software salesman, or a happy programmer. I wish I could be a politician, a successful politician. In this society, in modern China, it seems that in this city called Huainan I’m living in America of the eighties and nineties. It seems I’m living twenty years behind the times other people live in. Some people still live at ease. Let me ask you: are you miserable living through all the backstabbing and scheming at your company? I think you’re torturing yourself by living like that, unwilling to change. Yes, you’re living, and what the hell does that have to do with me? You live at ease, and it makes me uneasy to watch. Fuck the gaokao. I think the whole thing is a joke. Screw the gaokao, goddamn it, and those teachers. Living in this school is torture. I know, not change, it can’t be changed. I know my online friends say this fits our national conditions. I know that’s right. Hundreds of millions of young Chinese are striving for China, and some of them have to be weeded out. I wrote about Chinese politics in one of my journal entries. I don’t want to talk about it, and there’s no need. Peace and unification are what development needs, and what the people hope for. I hate the gaokao, a pointless exam. Chinese people, so many have bet their lives on it. Yes, some have. But afterwards, don’t they go on living just fine? China’s gaokao is the imperial examination of the Sui and Tang dynasties: it pulls in huge numbers of intellectuals, and then… I won’t say… I’ll walk my own road and do my own thing. Why bother with so-called other people’s business?
