title: Off to Shanghai Again
content:
I’m leaving for Shanghai the day after tomorrow. It’s always like this: right before Chinese New Year, when everyone else is rushing home…I’m always heading out… I remember last year, 15 days before New Year, I also left for Shanghai, and then on the morning of New Year’s Eve I took the bullet train back. I was 16 then, and now I’m 17. Being on my own is great. Let me tell you how that trip felt. I rode from the first station all the way to the last. The seat across from me changed hands 4 times: someone got on at one stop and off at the next, then someone else got on, then got off at the next stop. I held my MP3 player and sat there without moving, listening to music and watching the scenery outside the window. It was a hard sleeper, and sitting in it was miserable. (The second time I took a train by myself was to Hefei last summer. That trip was super awkward. Someone mistook me for a ticket scalper… WTF…) I finally got to Shanghai a bit after 8 in the evening. I remember it was raining that day and really cold. The buses had basically stopped running, and there were no taxis either… I walked through the rain across several intersections. That was my first time in Shanghai… I flagged down a taxi, and the driver said he didn’t know that road… I flagged down a second one, and the driver said he’d give it a try… When I came back from Shanghai, I was afraid of being late and missing my train. The train was at 7, and I left the hotel at 4. I waited at the station for an hour before I could board. I’m going to Shanghai the day after tomorrow, and I’m not looking forward to it at all… I’m going for an exam… well, an interview to be precise, an interview for classes. (I’m still a minor, so I can’t be going for a job…) It looks like my ticket back is standing room only… Damn it, sigh~ what a disaster…

PS: I think one really pointless thing about personal blogs is this: someone writes about their own life, a diary-type post, and when they’re done they post it in some QQ group begging for clicks. I find that really meaningless, and then you look at the comments and they’re all lukewarm… It’s kind of boring. If you write an opinion piece or something, sure, post it and take a look, the comments are fine… but you’re posting even your diary~ isn’t that annoying…

title: Tired and Sleepy, Time to Wash Up and Go to Bed
content: After New Year I thought things over. I’m at a crossroads, and what I’m facing is a real decision, not just a choice, so I get it. I get all of it. I have no plans to shut down the blog, so it’ll keep running as usual. But the update frequency, what I write about and what I focus on will change a lot compared with last year. In the end you have to face things, face everything. Time to wash up and go to bed. I’ve been with my girlfriend these past few days, and being happy is tiring too. I’m tired, I’m sleepy, I’m going to wash up and sleep. In five more days I’m off to Shanghai again, and I know that once I go~ it’ll be half a year. I seem to have changed, but actually I haven’t. That’s what a buddy told me at our middle school reunion the day before yesterday. He felt it was a shame: we started on the same road, but then went our separate ways. I go my way, he goes his. What do we live for? To keep going, to chase our dreams, for the people who love us, and for the people we love.

title: The World's Healthiest Daily Schedule
content:
** **

**7:30: Get up.** Researchers at the University of Westminster in the UK found that people who get up between 5:22 and 7:21 in the morning have higher levels of a substance in their blood that can cause heart disease, so getting up after 7:21 is better for your health.

Turn on the lamp. “As soon as you wake up, turn on the light. This resets your body clock and adjusts your sleep and wake patterns,” says Jim Horne, a professor at Loughborough University’s Sleep Research Centre.

Drink a glass of water. Water is essential for the thousands upon thousands of chemical reactions in your body. A glass of plain water in the morning makes up for the dehydration of the night.

7:30–8:00: Brush your teeth before breakfast. “Brushing before breakfast helps prevent tooth erosion, because brushing coats your teeth in a protective layer of fluoride. Otherwise, wait until half an hour after breakfast to brush,” says Gordon Watkins, a health and safety researcher at the British Dental Association.

8:00–8:30: Eat breakfast. “You have to eat breakfast, because it helps keep your blood sugar stable,” says Kevin Whelan, a dietitian at King’s College London. For breakfast you can have things like oatmeal, which have a low glycemic index.

8:30–9:00: Avoid exercise. Researchers at Brunel University found that athletes who train in the morning are more likely to catch illnesses, because the immune system is at its weakest at this time. Walk to work. Researchers at the University of Massachusetts Medical School found that people who walk every day are 25% less likely to catch a cold than people who sit all day and don’t exercise.

9:30: Start the hardest work of the day. Researchers at a New York sleep center found that most people’s minds are sharpest in the first hour or two after waking.

10:30: Give your eyes a break from the screen. If you work at a computer, rest your eyes for 3 minutes for every hour of work.

11:00: Eat some fruit. This is a good way to deal with a dip in blood sugar. Eat an orange or some red fruit; this boosts both your iron and your vitamin C.

13:00: Add some beans to your bread. You need a tasty lunch that releases energy slowly. “Baked beans are rich in fiber, and the tomato sauce can count as part of your vegetables,” says Dr. Whelan.

14:30–15:30: Take a short nap. A study by a university in Athens found that people who nap for 30 minutes or more at midday, at least 3 times a week, have a 37% lower chance of dying from heart disease.

16:00: Have a yogurt. This helps stabilize your blood sugar. Having some yogurt between your three daily meals is good for your heart.

17:00–19:00: Exercise. According to your body clock, this is the best time to exercise, says Reeve Nick, a sports science doctor at the University of Sheffield.

19:30: Eat a light dinner. Eating too much at dinner raises your blood sugar, puts extra strain on your digestive system, and disturbs your sleep. Eat more vegetables at dinner and fewer high-calorie, high-protein foods. Eat slowly and chew well.

21:45: Watch some TV. Watching a bit of TV to relax at this time helps you sleep, but try not to watch TV lying in bed, since that hurts your sleep quality.

23:00: Take a hot bath. “A slight drop in body temperature helps you relax and fall asleep,” says Professor Jim Horne of Loughborough University’s Sleep Research Centre.

23:30: Go to bed. If you get up at 7:30 in the morning, going to sleep now gets you a full 8 hours of sleep.

Any attempt to change your body clock will leave your body with mysterious illnesses, and if you regret it 20 or 30 years later, it’ll be too late.

1. 9–11 p.m. is detox time for the immune system (lymph). Stay calm or listen to music during this time.

2. 11 p.m.–1 a.m. is detox time for the liver, which has to happen during deep sleep.

3. 1–3 a.m. is detox time for the gallbladder, same as above.

4. 3–5 a.m. is detox time for the lungs. That’s why people with a cough cough hardest during these hours: the detox has reached the lungs. Don’t take cough medicine, so you don’t stop the waste from being cleared out.

5. 5–7 a.m. is detox time for the large intestine. Go to the bathroom and have a bowel movement.

6. 7–9 a.m. is when the small intestine absorbs the most nutrients, so eat breakfast. People recovering from illness should eat early, before 6:30; people looking after their health, before 7:30. People who skip breakfast should change the habit; even eating at 9 or 10 is better than not eating at all.

7. Midnight to 4 a.m. is when the spine makes blood. You must be sound asleep; don’t stay up late.

Remember this healthy daily schedule, plan your life well, and make your life rich and colorful!

title: Installing the DirectAdmin Panel on a CentOS VPS
content:
I finally bought a VPS, and only got it set up today… I bought a license for the DirectAdmin panel and installed it. I spent two hours wrestling with it before it finally worked, and then the Chinese localization ran into problems. Thankfully the expert Chuanzhang fixed it for me~~ hehe~~ Now let me explain how to install the DirectAdmin panel on CentOS 5.5. First you need a clean CentOS system. I chose

Step 1: install the CentOS packages you need. First run

yum update –y

Then run

yum -y  install gcc gcc-c++ flex make perl quota automaker

PS: Depending on the system, some VPSes are missing a lot of packages, so install whatever the prompts tell you to. Step 2: CentOS comes with the Unix version of httpd, but DirectAdmin needs a clean system to install, so before installing you have to uninstall web components like httpd, php and mysql

yum remove httpd* php* mysql* -y

Step 3: the actual installation. Run this command to get the install script

wget http://www.directadmin.com/setup.sh

Make the script executable

chmod +x setup.sh

Run the script

./setup.sh

Once it’s running it asks you for your license details and so on, for example: Please enter your Client ID : Please enter your License ID : Please enter your hostname (server.domain.com) as well as the licensed IP address and so on! When it got to “Enter your choice (1 or 2):” I chose 2. After that it should be just typing y and pressing Enter. There’s a step mentioned online here that I never ran into, so I’ll skip it…… /* On a dedicated server you’re done at this point, but on a VPS the panel won’t open yet. There’s one more step: configure the network device. Run the ifconfig command to see your VPS’s IP address. The device that IP address is bound to is what we need to note down, for example venet0:0 (OpenVZ VPSes need this change, Xen doesn’t). The IP device I found during my install was also venet0:0, so it’s probably the same for most VPSes! Open the DirectAdmin config file /usr/local/directadmin/conf/directadmin.conf with vi

Find something like ethernet_dev=***, change the value after the equals sign to the venet0:0 we just looked up, then save and exit vi. */ Then reboot Linux so the changes take effect. After the reboot, enter http://ip:2222 in your browser. If you see a login box, DirectAdmin has been installed successfully. (Make sure you reboot! Unlucky me didn’t, and so the control panel wouldn’t open.) Next up is the Chinese localization for the DirectAdmin panel. First download a tool, fzftp.rar , and use it to connect to the VPS. Then download the language pack lang.zip and copy the files in the language pack over the ones in

and that’s it. Edit user.conf

and that’s it. All done~ Ta-da…… the brand-new DirectAdmin panel appears before your eyes!

One last plug: I’m still sharing this VPS with others. I’ll post the specific resource plans in a few days. PS: Could everyone please ping godvps.net to test the speed~ and let me know how it is. My little blog will move to the VPS in a few days, so please bear with me

Enter “rouser jiankongbao auth”, then save and quit. (This is v3c authentication, adding a read-only account as follows: rouser jiankongbao auth. What that line means: in v3c, “rouser” indicates a read-only account type, the following “jiankongbao” is the chosen username, and the “auth” after it says authentication is required.) Step two: we need to create the user jiankongbao. For that we need the file /var/net-snmp/snmpd.conf, which is loaded automatically when snmpd starts. Since we haven’t run snmp yet, create the file by hand with these commands:

(This line creates a user named “jiankongbao” with the password “mypassword”, using MD5 for encrypted transmission. One reminder: the password must be at least 8 bytes long. That’s required by the SNMP protocol; if it’s shorter than 8 bytes, communication won’t work.) Finally, start snmp

title: Notes from the Second Day of Mid-Autumn
content:
This morning I was groggy, and my stomach suddenly hurt like crazy~~ went to the bathroom to deal with it~~ turned out to be diarrhea. Then I slept until 10, got up, read a bit and went online.

After lunch I got in touch with Hu Di and said we should go see Under the Hawthorn Tree. At first he agreed. I said 4 o’clock, and he said OK.

A little after three in the afternoon I was in the shower, rubbing shampoo all over my head, when suddenly the water got cut off…… Ugh, how awkward. I yelled for my dad, and we used the house’s backup water supply, a kettle of water we’d stored earlier, to get through it. I barely managed to finish my shower.

Then I sat around waiting for Hu Di to call. At 4 he called and said he wasn’t coming. Talk about a facepalm. Luckily I hadn’t bought the tickets yet……

After that I said we could switch movies, and he said he wanted to see Inception…… Didn’t we just see it a few days ago?…… Hu Di was doing it for some girl…… I was speechless……

So I bought a ticket by myself and watched the movie with two girls. And then…… before the movie started, I ran into Tao Xue, then Huang Mengjia, then Gao Di…… Huainan sure is a small place.

Getting my hair cut in the afternoon was even more awkward. I waited about half an hour. If I’d known, I would’ve just picked a stylist…… damn…… wasted so much time!

The movie was really long~ and really slow, so by the end it only moved me a tiny bit. I still remember that other film, called something like Your and My First Love, a Japanese film. If it had been in Chinese it would’ve been pretty good. They’re all tragic love stories.

Sigh, it’s left me really tired now. I want to sleep.

Even after getting home I can’t go online. I have to memorize vocabulary first.

Read my English book. Right now there are only three things in my head:

1.English

2.Programming and algorithms

3.Websites

Everything else isn’t essential anymore~

title: My Literary Side
content:
So many thoughts I want to write down. The blog has been neglected for a long time, and most of the time it’s just complaints, endless complaints.

Tonight my babe was picking a fight with me, so I went along with it. Nothing I can do, it’s always like this. After fighting for so long, I’ve slowly stopped losing my temper, because only one person can be angry at a time. If both people get angry, there’s no way to keep the relationship going. Isn’t that how life is? When the rules hold you in place, all you can do is obey, not rebel. I’ve said this countless times and explained it in detail N times, but love is like this: no matter how much plain white rice you’ve eaten, you still have to keep eating your plain white rice to fill your stomach, and the same goes for love. Not a single day without worry. That’s life. You hope nobody bothers you while you live your life, but someone is meddling in everything you do. I’ve slowly gotten used to life not going my way. I’ve slowly come out of the low I hit during that period in Shanghai. Taking the TOEFL time after time, waiting through those days for yet another low score, that feeling of letdown, I’ve slowly gotten used to failing too. When success does show up, numb as I am, all I can do is smile and give life a “heh.”

Two Years

From the end of June 2011 to the end of June 2013, it’s been two years. I rarely talk to others about my private life. Like I wrote in an old journal entry, I buried myself and then dug myself back out. I don’t bring up the dark stuff from the past anymore. Even at the dinner table over drinks, I rarely tell anyone about my love life. My life now, the person who belongs to me now, now, later, in the future, until the end of the world, I’m very satisfied with all of it, so I don’t want anyone else to disturb it or meddle in it. Two years. If you got to know me again now, you’d find my personality has completely changed. A brand-new me would make you, who’s used to the old me, very uncomfortable. I’m not so bashful anymore. One is one, two is two. What I don’t like, I still don’t like. I’m not used to forcing things, but I follow the rules and obey orders. Sometimes, for my own sake, I’ll force a smile. Heh, that’s how society goes. You just go with the flow. In these two years, I’ve learned to find my own way around unfamiliar cities.

Love

In these two years I found true love, and it has lasted until today. That’s no accident. It was meant to be. I don’t want to say much about her and me. After all, it’s a secret in my heart, one I want to keep forever. You’ve never seen us fight, but it really does happen that often. Still, I have my own way of handling it. I’ve figured out your temper, but I can’t stop it from happening. Maybe that’s what love is.

School

Deep down I always tell myself that gold will always shine. Coming here was a choice I had no way out of. Even if I hate it, I have to learn to enjoy it. Maybe we got too much happiness before, and that’s why today we have to give more than others. With no temper left, I can only slowly learn to grieve inside, but I still keep forcing a smile. That’s what being a man is. What do you think? Right? High school: in 2010, during my second year, I took a leave of absence and stayed home. How many times did I go back while Class 8 was still around? Twice? Or three times? Slowly, up to today, I’ve found that it was probably always going to end up like this. A distance just formed between us, for good. Jin Yunheng, hope I didn’t get that wrong, Liu Ben, Cheng Xi, and others. Maybe I can still, after all these years away, I can still remember their names. That distance is always so far. A high school reunion once? Twice? Maybe we’re just not the same kind of people, and we can’t walk the same road. I didn’t keep in touch with you guys. I don’t know, if one day in the future I reach out to you, whether I’ll still be able to get you to come out. Every time I call you, I can feel that distance.

Middle School

Luckily I still have friends from middle school I can get in touch with, people I can still count on. Sometimes you’ll notice that I procrastinate. Sorry, I do. People who know me will understand. As long as you’re my friend, you’ll find that whatever you ask me to do, I’ll get it done carefully for you. Don’t worry, I won’t leave a friend hanging, you know what I mean, Hu Di, Fu Yu… One or two true friends are enough. You don’t need a ton of phone numbers. When you need me, I’ll give everything I’ve got. All that’s left from middle school are people I can make small talk with, chat with on QQ now and then, or don’t contact at all. What the teacher told us back then really came true. The ones I lost touch with, I haven’t contacted in 8 years.

Elementary School

Of the people from elementary school I’m still in touch with, the closest one is Xie Yi. We still run into each other at school now and then, but in a few more months I probably won’t see him anymore, haha. Then there’s Ding Ke. We saw each other a lot this Dragon Boat Festival. We were classmates, but I feel like we didn’t really know each other that well. Most of the time, it’s only after graduation that you realize how precious that bond is. We didn’t notice it before. Then there are my other elementary school classmates, Men Yun and Nie Bowen. My memories of you two are still stuck in elementary school. No need to say much more. Let my memories stay in elementary school. No matter what you’ve become today, in my eyes you still look like you did back then, and that’s how I’ll keep remembering you.

Coldness

If you’ve spent time around me, have you noticed how strange my personality is? Hot one moment and cold the next, that’s just how unpredictable I am. Sometimes when you ask me something, I’ll say nothing at all, and sometimes I’ll answer you warmly. That’s me. That’s how my personality was formed, just like yours has its own character. It might change in the future, but I don’t know whether it will change again. You may have asked where I went to school, or how I’m doing now. Deep down, I just don’t want to tell you. What I’ve learned these past few years comes down to two golden words: stay silent. Silence is the simplest answer. At the end of 2011, I remember the time I went to see a psychologist. Everyone has some kind of mental illness, they just don’t want to admit it. From that day on, I started to change myself. Think about it: when your own parents start doubting your dream, do you still have any reason to keep going? I’m also someone who gets scared after the fact, and my courage has slowly been worn away to nothing. If you’ve read this far, you may not be used to my writing style, but I’ve always written like this, and that hasn’t changed. I deleted all my old posts from my QQ Zone, so you can’t see how I used to write. I’ve changed a lot since then. Sigh, I’ve also gotten worse and worse. Consider this one of my lousy essays. Lastly, yesterday’s you and me, we’re doing just fine.

title: Awkward! The Indie Blogger Roll Call
content:
The indie blogger roll call. This thing everyone got sick of on QQ Zone has now spread to indie blogs. Uh, you know what, I got tagged by TTkea and yumao. Maozi’s version is in traditional characters, uh, which looks so awkward to me. OK, here we go

Rules: 1. Answer the questions below seriously and truthfully 2. Look back carefully at how your blog has grown, then answer the questions from rule 1 3. Get sentimental if you can 4. Feel free to add your own questions or modify the questions 5. After answering, pass this on to 3 blogs from your blogroll, and urge them to answer and keep passing it on 6. If you get tagged, finish as soon as you can, then pass it to others 7. Nobody gains anything from this, it’s just a trip down memory lane 8. Whoever gets tagged copies everything below the rules 9. No tagging back, OK

  1. How long has your blog been around? Do you remember the day it officially launched?

My blog has been around for about 141 days. It officially launched on February 21, 2010. My first hosting account has the date on it. Come to think of it, I’ve switched hosts many times since.

  1. Will you keep your blog going?

Absolutely. I’ll keep it going forever. Some other major reason might force me to shut it down, but I believe I can keep at it.

  1. If one day you gave up on your blog, what do you think the reason would be?

A major reason: I’m gone, or I’ve moved somewhere else, or I’m too broke to afford a blog, and so on…… There are lots of possible reasons……

  1. Did you have any other blog before your indie blog?

Does QQ Zone count? QQ Zone felt like garbage. Oh, and I remember having a Google Sites page, but it got XX’d, so I stopped. After that I had one on a business-blog site called Qibowang, kept it up for a while, and then abandoned it.

  1. Do you remember your first domain?

It’s this one, blueandhack.com

  1. What does your first domain mean?

It’s my one-of-a-kind ID online, so if you google blueandhack, it’s all me…… unless one day I get famous and someone impersonates me!

  1. Do you remember who your first link exchange was with? How are things between you now?

I remember. It was Buxin Ercai. He was the first one to leave a comment on my site and the first to swap links with me. I have no idea how he found me, heh. We haven’t been in touch for a long time, but we still link to each other~

  1. How did you feel when your blog got its first comment?

How did I feel! How do I put it~ it was complicated. Mostly I wondered how he’d found me~ uh~ I was baffled~ Overall I was really happy that someone could get to know me.

  1. You’ve spent a lot of your time on your blog. Have you ever regretted it?

No regrets! To help me set foot on American soil, ideally~ I want to turn my blog into a portal~ That’s my grand dream!

  1. Do you think friends you make through blogging are reliable? Do you trust them?

To quote Maozi: “Why wouldn’t they be reliable? Why wouldn’t I trust them??”

  1. If one day a blogging friend, or you yourself, had to leave this circle for some special reason, would you still come back to visit?

I’d come back. After all, I’ve put a lot of feeling into it. I’ll always miss the indie blogging scene

  1. Why did you start your blog?

Honestly, my reasons for starting a blog weren’t all that pure. It was for applying to American universities. I hope my blog can help me out and give me a hand. The blog serves everyone, but to quote someone else: “A blog is written for yourself to read”

  1. Has your reason for running your blog changed?

Mainly for fun, and secondly to serve everyone

  1. Does your blog bring you a lot of happiness?

Now it’s not just happiness. Sometimes it’s nerve-racking, like when the server goes down. Basically, my moods move with my blog.

  1. Do you feel OK if you go a day without visiting your blog?

Well, the first thing I do when I turn on my computer is log in to my blog and check the comments……

  1. Are there people from your real life who interact with you on your blog?

Not really. None of my friends are into this stuff. They’re all about to take the gaokao, the college entrance exam……

  1. How many of your real-life friends know you have a blog?

Pretty much all of them, but not one has ever left a comment. They say commenting is too much trouble~ I give up~

  1. What would you like to say to your blogging friends?

To quote Maozi again: “I’m a newbie, but I’m working hard to do better”

  1. What are you right now? Working? Or a student?

A student, of course. Not many middle-aged guys are into this kind of thing, right……

  1. Who are you going to pass this on to?

Well, I won’t drag too many people into this. I’ll pass it to Crazylin, hey33 and Brother Dahui, just these three~ hehe. If I think of anyone else, I’ll add them. HOHO, I’ll get them all in trouble and feel no guilt! (^__^) If they don’t see it, oh well! Actually, let me add one more: Qianshuiyu~

content: For a whole month now I’ve been going to bed around this time. Well, technically it’s already yesterday, heh. title: Another Year, a Year Gone By
content:
Time really flies. Writing this post feels a bit heavy.

A year has passed. Today I went to a buddy’s birthday dinner. Eight of us, not many, not few. Last year, I remember it was September 3rd (this year we celebrated early because of classes), a few of us buddies got together, and today we got together again. In a year, not much has changed, it’s just that I really miss my classmates.

I haven’t been to school in two months, and there’s a good chance I won’t go this semester. I’m busy with all the exams for going abroad. There aren’t that many really, just a few. I don’t want to go back and visit school because I don’t like the teachers there. They’re annoying, really unbearable.

Today’s conversation was all just chitchat. Since they have class tomorrow, nobody drank, heh. After dinner we went to a pool hall and played for a while, then everyone headed home.

The guys have all changed~ grown up, I guess. After all, we’re seniors in high school now, so I need to work hard too.

Four months of hard work, then an offer from UCB, and I’ll be completely satisfied. No, not satisfied. MIT is my ultimate goal.

I hate China’s exam-oriented education. Senior year, no foreign prep program, studying every subject there is. That’s the tragedy of an ordinary high school.

I’m done complaining. Be sunnier, change myself!

Here are some PS’s:

Haven’t had coffee in ages~ Today I’m getting an iced one, and I’ll go out for a walk every day when I’ve got nothing to do.

My blog has now moved to a VPS, so everyone is welcome to test its speed!

Let me talk about the move. It was actually pretty simple. My old blog was hosted at Qingyun with a CP panel, and the new one uses a DA panel. The move had a few small hiccups.

First, log in to my CP panel and pack up and compress the whole root directory.

Then use putty for the transfer. You need ssh for this, so if you don’t have ssh enabled this method won’t work for you…

Next enter your username and password (they won’t be shown in plain text)

Then you’ll get a command line. Right after that, enter

ls

Then you’ll see the directory listing. Find the public_html directory

Enter cd public_html

Right after that, enter wget http://XXXXXX/wordpress.zip (the address is your blog’s address, adjust to your situation)

At this point, the wordpress.zip archive from the old host gets downloaded to the new host.

Then enter logoout to exit

One more reminder: don’t point the domain to the new host before the transfer, that makes the download easier.

Then go to the new host’s root directory, unzip wordpress.zip, and everything’s OK.

After that comes MYSQL

MYSQL: I first backed up the database in the CP panel, then created a new account in the DA panel and imported the SQL, and that’s it. This was written pretty casually… heh

10.11.2015 update

Later I went to UofA, and I’m pretty happy with how it turned out. It just took four years. You can do a lot in four years, but I kept at it, and maybe fifty years from now I’ll be able to tell myself I have no regrets.

title: One Year of Independent Blogging
content:
I registered the domain on February 20, 2010. This time last year, after coming back from Shanghai, I set up my own personal independent blog, and I was super excited. Now, I’m in Shanghai.

I once thought about writing a post on what I’ve learned building a site, but I decided against it. I’m no site-building guru. The real gurus all keep quiet, living on the web, low-key, writing their own code and charting their own path.

One year of independent blogging. I’ve actually gained a lot this year. First, I got to know a whole lot of fellow independent bloggers, and I got into HTML, CSS, PHP and MySQL. I got a rough grasp of WordPress theme design and WordPress customization, and from building the site I even made a bit of money.

The road of an independent blog is a hard one, and pretty complicated. This time last year I bought hosting and a domain. The hosting was from 5V55 and the domain from Xinnet. Back then I didn’t know what GoDaddy was, what PHP hosting was, what a Linux host was. I was a total newbie who knew nothing. I remember when I was still in school, I’d stay up until 3 a.m. fighting with problems on my blog, and so on. Later I moved the domain to GoDaddy and switched the hosting to a VPS.

This year I switched WordPress themes 5 times, and two of them were my own. When I first started I knew nothing, not even HTML. Later, with guidance from online friends and my own digging, I slowly learned how to design and modify themes. WhiteLove is one theme I released.

Going from independent blogging to building sites, I learned what an impetuous world the internet is. Some people just love to show off, and some people stay very low-key. The show-offs end up badly; the low-key ones do well.

For the blog’s first anniversary, I thought about holding some kind of event, but I gave up on the idea because I don’t have the time right now, so no event.

Because WordPress.com is in a bad way in mainland China, a huge number of independent blogs sprang up. Some people build sites not for fun but for money. But money is very real, and very dirty. Some people who can’t build sites listen to the sales pitches of people who can, and slowly all their money gets hustled away, and in the end they have nothing to show for it. It’s a vicious circle online that many people find hard to escape, and in the end they not only waste their money but also lose a site that could have had a really bright future.

I’ve drifted pretty far from independent blogging. Actually there’s a lot more I could say, but some of it I’d rather not.

One year of independent blogging. Not a long time, but the road is long.

Writing the blog has gotten a bit tiring lately, but I’ll keep at it.

title: Approved for Google AdSense! The Good and the Bad Arrive Together~ Orz
content:
Yesterday, with nothing to do, I opened my Gmail

and this email was sitting in my inbox. I was stunned. I’d only applied the day before yesterday, and the reply came today~ Then I saw “Welcome to…” WOW!!! I made it~ After such a long time, I finally got approved~ 4 months~

Below are the rejection emails from my Google AdSense applications, for your viewing pleasure

Eight of them in total. The first batch were rejections over the type of site, and then came rejections because my site was down. Sigh~ each one more tragic than the last~ Yesterday I finally got in, and I’m over the moon~ HOHO~

The Baidu ad network approved me the week before last. Baidu approving me was only right~ heh~ But Baidu wasn’t smooth sailing either: three rejections in a row, then approved on the fourth try.

I figure the rejections had their reasons. Baidu seems to care about how many pages are indexed, and Google seems to care about the age of the domain. When I applied to Baidu, they had already indexed 200-something pages, whereas before it was only a dozen or so. Once it hit 200, Baidu approved me~ Google kept saying the site type wasn’t right. I figured the domain just hadn’t been registered long enough, so I kept waiting, and it turned out pretty much the way Little M said: Google approves you in the third month after the domain is registered. This is just my guess, probably not worth much as a reference… heh~

From now on I’ll write blog posts properly~ My plan is two updates a week~

I haven’t written much these past two months, but my blog is still holding at 50+ IPs a day. Not bad! Almost all of it comes from search engines, because my blog has a very detailed post on getting around the Great Firewall~ HOHO~

Speaking of which, that firewall post needs an update too~

Anyway, today I’m still basking in the joy of getting approved for Google AdSense~ o(∩_∩)o

I didn’t get to bed until 3 a.m. today, because manually minifying my CSS and JS made the site’s theme completely disappear. It turned into an ultra-minimal theme of plain white boxes, and no matter how I debugged it I couldn’t fix it (cause unknown, I’m still looking into it). So I had no choice but to delete all the files and the database (why did I delete the database~ I must have been out of it), and then it was uploading, debugging, tweaking the theme, adding plugins (in a few days I’ll share the plugins I use with everyone), and so on. By the time it was all sorted it was past 3, then I went to sleep. Uh~ this morning I had to drink two packets of instant coffee to stay awake~ ugh~

Truly, the good and the bad came together. But in the end it all worked out, and everything’s safe and sound~ heh

Finally, I wish everyone luck getting approved by Baidu’s and Google’s ad networks~ (and a special shout-out to my classmate Little Lu!!!)

title: Peach-Blossom Snow in March, a Beautiful Mood in April
content:
Peach-blossom snow in March rustles down outside the window; a beautiful April mood leaps up in my heart~

—A note

Drifting, the snow is drifting, drifting so beautifully, and it slowly calms people’s hearts. Let me, in this season, spring, grow slowly like a sprouting seed, so that in these days of rapid growth I don’t carelessly grow crooked and lose my shape.

April hasn’t come yet, but I’m looking forward to it, longing for April’s bright days. The drifting snow of March slowly quiets this place, giving us enough time to think about the meaning of life and the meaning of growing up. Yes, April holds an even more beautiful mood.

Reading this season: cold and dry, and a bit dull too. A burst of snow brings a certain mood, as if a bit more warmth, a bit more moisture, and the season’s old memories are wiped away.

It’s as if this is the first time I’ve seen snow in March, as if the trees are just beginning to bud, as if the peach blossoms are opening too. A kind of curiosity and excitement leaps into my heart. In the past I was always rushing forward, head down, doing what I had to do, ignoring so many things around me, walking my own path, and yet I lost something. Numbness took over every corner of my heart, so feeling happy, having a beautiful mood, became a rare thing. I haven’t felt it in so long. I’m looking forward to it, enjoying it, and I hope it lasts……

Everyone walks their own path, but everyone reaches a different end. Some people enjoy it, some suffer through it. A mood makes us feel things differently and get different things out of life. Why not enjoy it? Maybe, busy with our own affairs, busy with the trivia around us, busy being busy with what we call our busy work, we forget what life is really about. We start to worry, and then the heart starts to die. One day you’re in the graveyard, and you arrive in heaven.

In heaven, someone asks you: “What were you doing with your life?”

You might say: “I was busy.”

“Busy with what?”

“Busy with what I had to be busy with.”

“And what was that?”

“Just busy stuff……” And then there’s nothing left to say.

“Have you ever felt a beautiful mood?”

“……No. Maybe back in elementary school. That was a long, long time ago……”

Two people in heaven, asking each other questions.

Look at this restless world, brush the dust off yourself, then lift your head, look into the distance, look all around, and enjoy it~

The snow of March

The mood of April……

Full of hope for the future, and earnestly enjoying the present.

title: In an Age of Reposts, How Many People Still Love Writing Their Own Stories?
content:
I’ve been running an indie blog for over six months now. In March I was a total newbie who couldn’t even install WordPress and had customer support do it for me. Now I’m a rookie who can handle a VPS and has his own theme.

Lately I’ve been wondering about something: why are there so many indie blogs? Why are so many people still stuck at the WordPress beginner stage……

In an age where reposting runs rampant, an age where people only write about trending topics, how many people still love writing their own stories? Put it this way: someone who loves writing their own stories has a successful blog. If you’re reposting news, that’s not called a blog. If you’re doing it for IPs and traffic, go ahead and repost all you want. All I’ll say is, you must be damn bored! (I admit I’ve done this myself)

How many people write their own stories, I don’t know. Most write about whatever is hot, and their blogs have no theme…… wandering aimlessly forever, until in the end all that’s left is an empty shell running WordPress.

Write your own stories, write your own views. Don’t write about things that have nothing to do with you or with your blog’s theme…… Don’t be so bored that you’ll write about anything……

A while ago, while I was working on my own blog theme and such…… I put together a few WordPress posts. I admit my blog also went down the wrong path before…… but I’ve fixed that now. For example, this post, Back to Top, the Perfect Version, was written for a certain kid…… he didn’t know how, so I wrote it up……

I’m planning a website…… I intend to make it one of the most famous sites of 2011. I have a lot of sites on my hands…… I don’t even know how to manage them all. My favorite symbol is this one……

To friends using WordPress, I want to say: WordPress is only a tool for blogging. What matters is your blog’s content.

If you started out wanting to write your own stories but ended up researching WordPress, snap out of it and get back to your posts…… Don’t waste your effort on WordPress skins…… Trust me, you’re worth it

Actually, modifying WordPress themes isn’t that hard. The main problem is that nobody has translated the most important WordPress resource, the Codex…… That’s a tragedy…… (I’m planning to start translating the Codex. It’s public, anyone can join in)

PS: About 360 vs. QQ, what I want to say is

360 is software made by the father of all rogueware with loads of venture capital. It never managed to make money, so now it’s going for broke, trying to use privacy to take down Tencent and the other antivirus makers. A leopard can’t change its spots. If 360 gets its way, it’s the users who will end up paying sooner or later.

I really do find 360 a bit of a gossip…… In its counterattack on QQ it even dragged up the business about Ma Huateng receiving XXX…… A tragedy for China’s IT industry.

My study-abroad plans have been pushed back a year, so I have plenty of time to prepare. In a year I’ll be 18.

title: On a Slow Journey, I Gaze at That Distant Lamp
content:
I hope my journey has a lamp like this too:

Deep in the night

Alone, quietly writing down my dreams

Dreams as dreamlike as dreams, mercilessly mocked

Dreaming my own dream

Looking down at my own feet

Gazing into the distance

Touching the glass close by

Turns out it’s still so far away

I know my journey has begun

A journey that will last a year

It’s long

But it’s also swift

That lamp is always lit

That tiny light

Seems visible only to those who know it

Watching it

Keeping it from going out

The best way is to fire it up with my heart

A kind of passion

Leaps from my chest with a pounding beat

Turning that tiny flame into a raging blaze

I see it

I see it even more clearly

I charge forward

Breaking through that transparent barrier

A slow journey

I run ahead

A long, long journey

I gaze at that distant lamp

I believe that I can finish my dreams……

title: Printing a Diamond in One Line
content:
I first saw this on pwhack‘s blog. He wrote it in Go, but for a classic exercise like this there are lots of ways to do it in C. So I wanted to see just how short the simplest version of this problem could get. And then I found this snippet

You might be wondering: what’s the * doing in printf()?

Actually, * is a modifier, and you can use it in both scanf() and printf(). In scanf, * means skip… For example:

scanf("%*d %*d %d",&n;); printf("%d",n);

So when you type 1 2 3, only n gets stored, and it prints 3 as normal. With * in printf(“%*d”，width,n);, because the order is * then d, width actually sets the output width of n, and n is what gets printed. For example: int n=3; scanf("%d",width); printf("%*d",width,n); When you type 2, it prints (空格)3

Maybe you’re asking what "*******"+2*(line>4? line-4:4-line) means?

If you look closely, it’s just a string pointer plus an int, in other words shifting the pointer. For example, when line=1 on the first row, 2*(line>4? line-4:4-line) comes out to 6, so the pointer to the 7-star string shifts by 6 and only one star gets printed. This is the shortest one-liner diamond I’ve ever seen. If you know a shorter one, tell me here.

title: My dream, I can to achieve her.
content:
Tonight I switched WordPress’s display language to EN, because reading it in Chinese was really bugging me… For a while now, I’d say about half a year, I’ve been thinking about a few questions, and in the last few days I think I’ve finally figured them out. Stay low-key, don’t be restless, stay calm and composed: I can’t do any of that. Last summer vacation, I remember it was last summer, that’s when I started to change, from a little kid who knew nothing to slowly understanding life, and it isn’t pretty. In 2009, before my freshman year of high school was even over, I got threatening messages from someone saying they’d come to my school to find me… I guess I was lucky that day, they didn’t find me, maybe because I left early. Then he kept leaving me messages and kept looking for me, saying that when he found me he’d beat me up. I was pretty scared at the time, and I couldn’t figure out why he wanted to beat me up. He just seemed to not like me. My guess was that someone had hired people to beat me up. I hadn’t offended anyone back then. The only person I’d offended was a girl who liked me and got turned down. I thought, no matter how much she hated me, she couldn’t possibly get someone to beat me up. Damn. Then I rounded up a bunch of people, ahem, buddies who’d come to help me the second they heard I was getting beaten up. Later the whole thing just fizzled out. Now a year has passed and I still haven’t been beaten up. I think whoever wanted to beat me up has long forgotten about it. My high school life, for me, has been over for a while now. When I was at school, life was really dull. Take New Year’s Day: the school had no events at all and didn’t allow classes to organize anything either. Our school had no events for seniors, while seniors at other schools all had events. We got very few days off. The school docked our holidays, squeezed our breaks, and it was all extra classes, classes and exams. That’s why I hate my high school. Compared with the other high schools in this city, principal, you’re not fucking human! To complete its “plain education” research project, our school had no multimedia equipment in the high school classrooms. Suuuper plain. I heard the project won’t end until 2012. I don’t think the project is worth studying anymore. Once they finish studying it in 2012, who’s going to look at it? My Chinese teachers: in two years of high school, I had two of them. We wrote weekly journals with no assigned topic, free to write whatever, so every time I wrote either rants about education or argumentative essays. What was the most fun time at high school? Goofing around with my buddies, wandering around the school. The school had no clubs at all, except for an arts and culture festival. The so-called arts and culture festival was just that one day. Since the school had no auditorium or anything, because it’s right next to the city center and space is really tight, we watched it out in the square. Damn, it was usually in November and freezing. Goofing around with my buddies, I don’t even know what we were goofing around doing. Going to internet cafes. I was the youngest of us… still underage, though of course I didn’t lack for internet access. The school had no heating… which I’ve never been able to understand. All I can say is, what the fuck are you researching with this “plain education,” damn, seriously, o(︶︿︶)o sigh. How do I put it, my high school was unlucky. For example, at the freshman-year sports meet, in the 400 meters, my leg cramped and I just collapsed on the track… At the sophomore-year sports meet, in the 4x100 relay, I dropped the baton… we came in dead last… because of me… My high school was a tragedy in other ways too: before freshman year was even over, the bike I’d paid 1,500 yuan for got stolen. Then I confessed to the girl I liked and got rejected… Then on the last exam of high school, I ranked near the bottom of my whole grade… and then, that was it. All through high school I was the class monitor. I’m really grateful to my homeroom teacher for not judging me with tinted glasses, ahem. My grades at school were really bad, and my homeroom teacher didn’t hand out positions based on grades. At least that was something. …Sigh, and that’s how high school ended. Someday we’ll get together, have some fun, and then everyone will go their separate ways. Writing this post, I just feel it’s time for me to wake up… Burn, my Cosmo~~

My dream,I can to achieve her.

To match the title, ahem: one person’s dream, one person walks it.

title: Sea Fog
content:
A poem:

When the fishing boat sails across the sea;

When the petrel soars above the sea;

When the sun fades from sight……

Fog,

slowly spreads over the sea,

the fishing boat can’t help but lose its way,

    aimlessly searching for a path,

the petrel circles in the sky,

    searching for a reef to land on;

Fog,

the smell of the sea fills the mind,

making you more and more restless,

the fishing boat slowly comes to a stop,

    calm, calm, the sea has fallen asleep,

the petrel finds a reef,

    she stops, and slowly drifts into dreams on the calm sea……

“Whoosh” “whoosh,” the waves slap the fishing boat;

“Whoosh” “whoosh,” the waves strike the reef;

Suddenly the fishing boat moves, the fishing boat sails, threading through the sea fog.

The petrel’s wings are soaked, she falls into the sea,

yet she bravely takes off again to look for another,

—a tall reef.

The fog seems to have fallen for the sea,

                unwilling to part again.

The fishing boat looks for its home;

                the petrel looks for that reef to land on.

The next day,

the fishing boat comes to the shore,

and out steps an old Red Army veteran,

he looks east toward the sunrise, thinking about something,

in the afternoon he finds something on the shore,

—a petrel, a dead petrel.

One of her wings is gone,

the old Red Army veteran buries her by the sea,

letting her look out at the sea,

and somewhere on the sea,

—the fog has not yet lifted.

Written by Jianfeng Yiyu, November 2008

This is a poem I wrote at the end of ‘08. That was a long time ago, but I was still dreaming of changing my country back then!

title: A Sense of Belonging
content:
This isn’t the first time I’ve come home from somewhere else for Chinese New Year, and it won’t be the last. Anyone who’s human has a strong sense of belonging. “When folks from back home meet, their eyes fill with tears,” someone on the train said, half joking. On the 19th, the morning I got back, I went straight to bed as soon as I got home. I slept until the afternoon, ate something, then went back to sleep, and I kept sleeping for two days. I only got up to eat, ate in bed, and then went back to sleep. That’s how two days went by. So exhausted I couldn’t hold up, that’s how I felt. The whole train car was packed full, not a single free seat, so you could only stand, and if you could squeeze in somewhere to sit for a bit, you were doing great. I basically stood all the way from Shanghai to home, 11 hours in total. When I got off, my legs had gone stiff and I couldn’t lift them… And the car was really hot. It was snowing outside, and I was drenched in sweat. A sense of belonging is a feeling every person has. Animals have a sense of home too. I think any animal does. The Spring Festival travel rush, I just can’t take it. I was going to write this post properly, but forget it, I’ll just wrap it up quickly. Tomorrow a few classmates are getting together, my treat. We haven’t seen each other in a few months. We may never see each other again after this. That’s life. On the train, I knew that the person sitting across from me was someone I’d meet only once in this lifetime. There’s no chance we’ll ever meet again. As for finding a girlfriend, I have to say it’s a real pain. My situation is really unstable… sigh. A line from Chang Chen-yue’s “OK”:

Sometimes I just want a one-night stand. Put real feelings in, and I’m afraid I’ll lose my freedom

title: Helpless Tears
content:
I listened to “Mama! China,” a song written by two Chinese students studying in North America, and it stirred up endless thoughts, so I wrote this short poem. Faced with choosing between two paths of education, I’m honestly lost. How am I supposed to choose?

Helpless Tears

China,

our motherland,

the place that raised us.

China,

not yet a hundred years old,

China,

motherland,

mother,

I look at you,

and my heart aches without end,

should I weep,

or simply grieve.

Motherland,

I cannot shake your foundations,

those solid foundations of your education.

Mother,

you are my mother,

it was you who taught me everything,

and I,

now,

must kill your way of thinking,

my mother,

Mother China,

my mother,

China.

In 1949,

“Founding” rang through the hearts of all the nation’s people,

and yet,

the foundations of your education have stood for thousands of years of history,

they have festered,

but you won’t let your son bandage them for you,

you make me stand by and watch

the pain on your face,

and all I can do is weep……

2009-12-25

Afterword: Chinese people put great stock in foundations, so they truly can’t be shaken, or even talked about. But Chinese people are also willing to move and repair those foundations; it’s just that some of it is too abrupt, and goes too far. We live at the bottom end of the city hierarchy, so it’s no surprise that we think about these things. Still, we’re not the tired ones, unlike some people putting on a show over there for the big shots. That’s exhausting, and laughable too. But how many Chinese people will ever wake up? Everyone says college is heaven and high school is hell. Heh, I think China really is just China. While writing this, I truly cried. I’m really sad and upset. I can’t change anything, but I can be like Jingwei trying to fill the sea one pebble at a time. ——Written by Jianfeng Yiyu on the night of December 24, 2009 Second afterword: I thought this piece was pretty good, so I posted it. I wrote it myself, and honestly I wrote it in tears, really. I’m a bit lost. I admire the American education system, but I hope China’s will improve. Countless Chinese students are like political tools, pinned firmly in place by society. Are they puppets or marionettes? Who knows. China has no marches, no organized, disciplined protests. None. Not today, not tomorrow, not the day after. There won’t be any. The motherland is very young, not even grown up yet. What I hope for is that the motherland will live forever. The nation’s tragedy: when education fails, the nation is bound to fall. ——Something I hope never happens Yesterday I made a drawing that expresses how I see education. Honestly, I want to cry. I can’t find the way forward for education. Where does the motherland’s future development lie? Which way should I go? I don’t know We seem to get called angry young men~ So are you all cowards, then? Just like the lapdogs of the Qing government?

title: Silence
content: Late at night, I suddenly thought back to the bullet train home from the World Expo in 2010. I was still really naive then. It’s been three years, but I vaguely remember getting into an argument on the train with the daughter of one of my dad’s coworkers (the Expo trip was organized by my dad’s workplace). It got pretty heated, but now I can’t even remember what we were arguing about. The topic seems to have been education. I don’t know where I got the energy and nerve to argue back then. (I wonder where that girl got into college. Is Chinese education really as great as she praised it back then?) PS: I can still remember that I was mostly on the opposing side, criticizing and so on. Thinking it over carefully now, sometimes you need to stay silent. Even if you know, even if you understand, even if you’re an expert, the moment you argue with idiots, you only drag your own IQ down to their level. Me now, I’ve lost that impulsiveness and nerve. Sometimes I avoid the subject; in areas where I clearly know my stuff, I play dumb in front of others even though I understand. The more people I deal with, the less I want to make trouble for myself. Maybe that’s just how my mind works. Speak when it’s your turn to speak, and shut up when it isn’t. Talk less and do more. If you don’t understand, ask; don’t try to guess what other people mean. Treat yourself like a fool; after all, you’re not that smart. And remember: don’t try to be clever!

title: Recent Stories
content:
Yes, I’ve posted again! It’s already fall 2016, my third year in Tucson, and everything that happened in 2014 feels like it was just yesterday.

I know it’s been about a year since I wrote on this blog. Most of my time has gone into studying, so I can go home, so I can finish this choice early, one I partly regret and partly am glad about (the road of coming to the US to study). That’s why I chose to take classes over the summer.

Summer

Speaking of summer, in summer 2016 I went to Japan.


I was there for 5 days in total and had a great time. It was the happiest summer I’ve had, even though the summer classes were exhausting.

In August I came back to the US, thinking about moving, and I was actually pretty happy. But the day I got back in August and reached my old apartment, I was completely stunned. The place had been cleaned out: the lock was pried open, and most of the stuff I mentioned in my last post was gone. Three monitors, the router, the graphics card, the NAS (including the four hard drives in it and all the data). The most tragic part is that I didn’t have insurance, so what’s gone is gone. I called the police, but there’s not much hope, because there are no cameras anywhere in the complex.

Later I moved into a new place, got a DS916+ and a new router, and after that bought some parts and built myself a Hackintosh.

Back to school

Since I took summer classes, I was a sophomore when school started. This semester I’m taking about three major courses, and it’s going pretty well so far, except there’s so much homework that it eats up a lot of time. This semester I’m learning MIPS, a language I’d never studied before, and honestly I’m a bit lost in class. In earlier classes I could coast on what I already knew, but this one I really need to put work into.

This semester has been fun. It seems like as long as I’m learning a lot, I’m happy. On my birthday I was even lucky enough to see a rocket launch. A nice surprise.

Right now

The main thing right now is probably getting through next week’s exam, and going to the Tutoring Center more often to talk through homework.

I’ll write on this blog more from now on. Sometimes I have a lot I want to say, but in the end I just digest it all myself. I also need to remind myself to write more technical posts. After all, a lot of the time I can’t remember later why I wrote my own code the way I did, so I should write a post to keep a record.

PS: I’ve noticed my written Chinese has gotten really bad, especially punctuation. I have no idea where to put it anymore……

title: Separating a Ton of Phone Numbers with Commas
content:
Tonight I needed to text more than 50 people, so I thought of Wandoujia. I copied the numbers from Excel into Wandoujia to send them all at once with its group SMS feature. As it turned out, things weren’t as simple as I’d thought.

I copied from Excel into Notepad, and it pasted the Excel way, as a column, not as a single line. So I copied the column of numbers into Wandoujia, and the result left me shattered…

You can see it says it will be sent to one contact. What now? Was I supposed to add English commas one by one to separate them? I told myself I couldn’t do something that primitive. After all, I’m a code monkey!

Scouting the Way with C, Done in No Time

I know C and Java, but in the end I chose C to write this little program. First you create a character array to hold the huge pile of numbers. Then the whole program works by replacing newline characters with English commas.

Using C’s file functions, the numbers get written out to Output.txt. Aha! That makes things so much easier.
