title: Grateful for 17 Years
content:
Their kindness, I can never forget

I don’t have a legendary backstory, only an ordinary 17 years of life. Like everyone else, I live a life that keeps moving forward. Now I’m trying to give thanks for my seventeen years.

—A note

Seventeen years ago I was born, and from then on I started growing up, from a kid who could only bawl his eyes out into the quick-witted teenager I am now. On that long road, I don’t know how many times I fell before I became who I am today; I don’t know how much my parents gave to make me who I am today; I don’t know how many times each of my teachers scolded and taught me before I gained more good sense. What I do know is that it took countless falls, endless giving, and countless rounds of scolding and teaching to bring me to where I am today.

My parents: my mom holding my hand, my dad watching over me

A mother can’t be described by the word “great” alone; mostly you can only feel it with your heart. My earliest memories are all about my mother. She’s an essential character in so many of my childhood stories. The days when I was just learning to babble have gone blurry in my memory, but in my “Baby’s Growing-Up Diary” my mom once wrote: “Jiajia gets upset easily, but he’s very cute.” Reading that, I can’t help thinking that as a little kid I must have given Mom so, so much trouble.

When I first started remembering things, the year I was two, I went to Beijing with my parents and we lived there for half a year. Apart from spilling a big bottle of Coke on the train because I loved making mischief, and getting scolded by my parents for it, Beijing roast duck, and running all over the Beijing Zoo looking for a bathroom, I have pitifully few memories, and that’s it. When I was little, my mother raised me with endless patience and care, never complaining. I think every mother does this; it’s instinct that makes them do it. Yet I was always making trouble for Mom, leaving her to quietly clean up my messes. All I can say here is: “Thank you, Mother!”

In elementary school, I remember that public service ad “Mom, let me wash your feet” was everywhere, and our teachers kept telling us to learn to be grateful, so I copied what the kid in the ad did. Ha, it seems so childish now. I figured my mom would give that same gratified smile as the mom on TV. That day I filled a big basin with hot water, and since it was too heavy to carry, I dragged it all the way over to her, said “Mom, let me wash your feet,” pulled off her shoes and socks, and started washing her feet. Mom watched me with a big smile, but why couldn’t I feel like I was being grateful? That feeling was missing, and I couldn’t help feeling let down. I asked myself: what does it really mean to be grateful?

Elementary school was a time I’m proud of. I had a real talent for drawing, entered quite a few art competitions, and did very well in them. Every time I brought home a certificate or medal from a drawing contest, Mom would grin from ear to ear. Only then did I realize that repaying Mom with actions and with results is the best gift, the best way to say thank you! Mom’s smile let me taste the sweetness of gratitude.

My elementary school years went by fast. I grew up in happiness, and I grew up with scoldings and spankings. Here I have to talk about my father.

My father was a soldier, with a strong build and thick, solid hands. As a kid, whenever I did something wrong, I never escaped a scolding and a spanking from him. The one I remember most was in fourth grade. That year, so I could show off toys in front of the other kids, I secretly took 200 yuan from home. Where did I get the nerve? I was usually such a timid kid, and just for that bit of vanity I did something like that. I bought a whole lot of toys, and then my father found out. I said a classmate had bought them for me as a gift, so my father went and asked my classmate, and naturally the lie was exposed one day. I remember my father coming up to me that day and asking, “Where did all this stuff really come from?” “A classmate gave it to me.” I knew the lie would be exposed, but I stubbornly kept lying. “Smack!” My father slapped me across the face, and the tears started falling right away. “Waaah…” “No lying. I hate liars more than anything. If you do something, own up to it.” “He did give them to me.” But I still kept stubbornly making excuses. My father found a wooden ruler and whipped me with it. It hurt so much I started sobbing. “Still lying? I already went to the school and asked. You bought all of this yourself, didn’t you? Where did you get that much money? I told you not to lie and you keep on lying.” I had no choice but to confess. My father stopped hitting me and started having a proper talk with me. With tears running down my face, I felt deeply ashamed and listened carefully to every word he said. After that, I never “took” money from home again. I broke my bad habit of sneaking around, and I never again did something wrong just to show off. It’s been 7 years since that lesson from my father. My father taught me how to be a decent person, what’s right and what’s wrong, how to get along with friends. He taught me so, so much. Thinking about it, the gratitude wells up and I can’t help crying. What have I done to repay my father? Nothing! How have I shown my gratitude? I haven’t! My father has always treated me like a friend. He raised me without a single complaint. He quietly supports me and teaches me. He doesn’t have a mother’s tenderness, but he has a father’s strength. A father’s love is like a mountain! It moves me deeply.

My parents have always given me room to grow freely. Here I want to say: “Mom, Dad, thank you. I’ll never be able to repay all you’ve done for me in my whole life!” If I could, I’d give two hundred percent, so I’m working really hard now!

My elementary school homeroom teacher: she watched me all the way into middle school

My elementary school homeroom teacher, I can’t remember what she looked like anymore; her face only drifts vaguely before my eyes. Recently I flipped through my elementary school photos and found a picture of the two of us together. We’ve only seen each other a handful of times since. Now she’s gone to teach in another city and we’ve lost touch. Maybe in a few years we’ll meet again!

I remember it was the end of the last century when I started elementary school. As soon as I walked into the classroom I met my homeroom teacher. She was young, kind and full of energy. Our very first lesson in elementary school was “Love Our Motherland,” and curious as I was about school, I couldn’t wait for my future to begin.

One afternoon in second grade, my mom came to the school. All I knew was that my grades weren’t very good back then and my homework was always sloppy, so the teacher decided to call my parent in. Because I was being told off, I cried my heart out.

“He’s been very careless with his schoolwork lately. Look at his recent tests, each one worse than the last.”

I was bawling.

“Mm, lately he’s been playing with the kids in our compound until really late. I tell him off and he won’t listen, he just throws a fit,” my mom said.

“Oh, is that so?” The teacher looked me in the face and said, “You can’t keep doing this. Look at your grades. Aren’t you embarrassed? The other kids all have such good grades, and yours…”

I kept crying. All I know is that from then on I didn’t goof off as much, and my grades shot straight up. My homeroom teacher kept pushing me the whole way, and only when I got into a really good middle school did she finally stop worrying.

Six years of quiet guidance, six years of selfless giving, six years of asking nothing in return… After elementary school graduation, my classmates and I talked it over, pooled some money, and bought her a big cake that we brought over on Teachers’ Day. We all got together to celebrate with her, and that’s the day the photo was taken. The next year she moved away. For the Teachers’ Days in the years after that, I could only wish her well silently in my heart: “Ms. Wang, happy Teachers’ Day!” It’s been four years since I’ve said that to her in person, and I really regret it. My very first mentor, and now all I can thank her with is a wish, and I don’t even get the chance to do that. I choke up quietly.

“Ms. Wang, thank you! Thank you for six years of teaching me! Thank you! This is the only way I can show my gratitude, but it carries everything I feel.” These are words I never said when she was by my side, and now I can’t say them to her. Now I know: gratitude can’t wait. Don’t let a single minute or second slip away and leave you with regrets.

The one I call my life mentor: Mr. Lu, the man who pointed the way

He’s my teacher, my computer teacher. Meeting him was by chance, but it also seems it was bound to happen. Meeting Mr. Lu is the honor of my life.

Meeting him was pure chance. I was in eighth grade then, and because of a computer magazine I happened to buy at a newsstand, I got hooked on computers and kept digging into them on my own at home. But that digging had no direction; I was lost. Then my mom said to me: “I found you a place to learn about computers. Go. It’s better than fumbling around by yourself at home.”

So the next day I went there, and when I looked, wasn’t that Mr. Lu, who had taught me English before? I met him because I loved computers, and that was bound to happen, because he loves computers too, ha.

“What do you want to learn about computers?” he asked me with a smile.

“Programming!” My answer was quick and sure.

“Mm, programming is the foundation of computing. Let me teach you C, then!” And so he started teaching me…

Back then I was in middle school and knew nothing about programming. I learned it half-understanding, in a fog. Mr. Lu taught me the syntax of programming languages, typing out each example program on the computer, and then had me rewrite it again from memory. And so, following Mr. Lu’s lead, I grew bit by bit. Gradually he had me write some small games on my own, and I got completely absorbed in the world of computers and came to understand the magic of programming.

I didn’t like English, and since he’d taught me English long before, he knew me well. In middle school, every time I had an English test I went in grumbling. I resented it, I hated it, I was sick of teachers spouting grammar all class and boring recitations of the textbook. Mr. Lu knew exactly what I was thinking. One day he sat down next to me. “Come on, you’ve been writing code for so long, let’s read a little story and take a break.” I nodded. Then I sat down next to his computer, and he translated an English story for me in a really lively way. I can’t remember what the story was anymore, but I was completely captivated by the English he described, and from then on I got interested. From that point, the me who used to sleep through English class started taking notes, and the me who used to copy other people’s English homework started doing the exercises myself, translating them one by one. I had a goal back then: to be able to read lots and lots of English stories, and to read computer books in the original English. A lot of translated computer books are unsatisfying and leave you scratching your head, which is why I got that idea. Back then I didn’t even know the basic subject-verb-object pattern, and sometimes I’d put two bare verbs in a row in one sentence. Looking back now, I was ridiculous, but that’s just how it was. As an eighth grader, my English was worse than a sixth grader’s. I was an English idiot. I started from the most basic vocabulary, memorizing words from the middle school vocabulary list every day. Mr. Lu didn’t believe in rote memorization, though. He usually slipped in explanations and memorization of words while we translated English stories together, and that’s what I liked best. It was this way of teaching that got me interested in English. With my own willpower, I finally memorized all the words before the high school entrance exam. Mr. Lu has a blog, and it’s well known. I became a regular there, checking online every so often to see if he’d posted anything new. Now I’m subscribed to his blog and I’m a loyal reader. Sometimes I nitpick and offer suggestions.

In eighth grade I ran into problems I’d never faced before, and everything felt lost: lost in my feelings, lost in my studies, lost in how to deal with people, and so much more. I couldn’t find my way forward. Sometimes I really wanted to give up on everything I’d worked for and sink along with the classmates around me who’d already given up. But right then I met Mr. Lu, which was chance, and I met computers, which was meant to be. After that, with Mr. Lu’s guidance, I found a bright path. Through Mr. Lu I learned about Kai-Fu Lee, Steve Jobs, Shing-Tung Yau and others, people I’d never heard of or cared about before, and so I had farther, bigger goals. Because Mr. Lu’s kid had applied to an American university all on their own, without an agency, he encouraged me to go to college abroad too. It was something I’d never thought about, never dared to think about. Back then I knew nothing about studying abroad, but I was full of confidence. Later, on the high school entrance exam, my English score made a huge leap, from a paper where I used to get a dozen or so points to over a hundred (out of one hundred fifty). My heart overflowed with gratitude, and I said to Mr. Lu, “Thank you!”

With him it’s like being friends. We really click. It’s what you’d call a friendship across generations, ha. We’d dig into problems together and think through the details of programs together, and have a great time doing it, like a big kid and a little kid hanging out. That’s why learning English didn’t feel so tiring. Now that I’m in high school, because of schoolwork I rarely go to study with him, and I can only teach myself English and programming.

“Mr. Lu, thank you! When I look back on middle school, I see that I didn’t make a single wrong choice. From losing my drive and feeling lost, to getting hooked on computers, to meeting you and coming to love English, it all seems like a script that was already written, waiting for me to act it out. I’m just being wise after the fact; I’ve only put all this together now. Mr. Lu, you’re a great teacher I met on my way to growing up. Thank you again!”

Thanks to Taisha: for bringing back my dream of studying abroad!

After a year of high school, the me who had sharp edges in middle school got worn smooth. I lost my spark and could barely breathe under the heavy coursework. My middle school dream of studying abroad got buried in the back-and-forth between the bus stop and school, dull and helpless.

Lost once again. It was the second time I’d felt this way since middle school. It was like I couldn’t see the goal in the distance anymore. The goals I set for myself got shattered by failure again and again, and finally vanished in my parents’ sighs. The summer after tenth grade I worked at my mom’s shop, which let me feel the pressures of society even more, and the lost feeling grew even deeper! I was walking through a fog, every so often running into a utility pole I couldn’t see, leaving me battered and bleeding.

That’s when I realized I really had to find the sun ahead of me. If I kept going like this, I might wander into the sea and be swallowed by the noise. Time to wake up! … The summer of ‘09 dragged on forever. That day I was wandering aimlessly online and accidentally clicked a link: “Taisha Forum.” Ha, I laughed. “Taisha, ‘Too Dumb’? What kind of name is that? Let me take a look…” Out of curiosity I started browsing the threads, and found out it was a forum for discussing study-abroad applications and exams. The forum was huge and covered everything, so I added it to my IE favorites and registered an account.

So I went to the forum every day, because deep down I was still thinking about my dream of studying abroad. Seeing other people’s TOEFL scores made my eyes go red like a rabbit’s. Seeing other people get perfect SAT scores made me itch with envy. Seeing other people get offers from top American schools, I could only look on and wish. Then one day, after browsing the forum, I got my spirit back and wrote down my dream. I looked up at the sky, and I knew the future had saved a piece of sky for me to paint. “Is Mr. Lu’s guidance going to end with me, right here? Is my dream just going to die?” “No!” I rekindled my dream of studying abroad, and it was all because of Taisha. Because of Taisha, I had the will to keep chasing this dream again. It relit the lamp in my heart that had gone out. May it be the guiding light for me from now on!

After that summer I started preparing for the TOEFL, and I talked with my parents about studying abroad. They were very supportive. Before, I didn’t have the courage to bring this up with them, because they thought it was better to go to college in China. Taisha gave me that courage. Thank you! Even though I’ve only known Taisha for a few months, it’s been changing everything about me and pushing me forward. “Thank you, Taisha. I met you at the most important moment! When I was lost, you showed me the way! Thank you for providing this place to share. You let me start my dream over again. Thank you!”

A curtain call that isn’t the end

Without a legendary backstory, all I can do is work step by step to get everything I want, and finish my dream drop of sweat by drop of sweat. Thank you, Mom and Dad, for giving me this small life and a body of my own; thank you, teachers, for giving me my own mind and letting me swim in the ocean of books; thank you, Taisha, for helping me find the dream I once had! Maybe someday down the road, when I look back on the past, I won’t regret my choices. I believe: “Your mission in life is to fulfill your very first dream!” The road ahead is long, like a play with no ending. I’ll always be standing on the stage, giving it my best performance, and the curtain will never fall.

Thank you all for your kindness, including the people I haven’t mentioned who have helped me. Thank you! Everything you’ve done for me over the past 17 years I’ll keep in my heart. All those little things have gathered in me and become an ocean. On some nights, looking up at the stars, I’ll find myself in tears, because your kindness, drop by drop, moves me again and again. I can’t thank each of you in words, but I’ll bless you in my heart. May heaven watch over you, and may gratitude keep being passed on.

My pen name: Jianfeng Yiyu

January 19, 2010

title: What I Need to Get Done This Week
content: Today’s post is mostly about what I need to do over the next two days and through this weekend. First, there’s the Reading Month event next Monday, and the student union president asked me to write a speech to give as the student representative. Then there’s shooting a micro-film this weekend. Then there’s setting up a verified Weibo account for the school. They’ve asked me to maintain and manage the school’s Weibo, plus the WeChat platform. Looking at all these tasks, I’ve got my hands full. Keep a low profile and just get things done: that’s always been my rule. No showing off. I didn’t go to the library today because I was in the dorm at noon applying for the Weibo account, so I didn’t make it. Tomorrow I’ll get back to my plan. Come on, me!

title: This Is Life
content: If you feel lonely, that’s right, it’s your chance to get to know yourself. If you feel misunderstood, that’s right, it’s your chance to see who your friends really are. If you feel surrounded by darkness, that’s right, it’s your chance to find the light. If you feel helpless, that’s right, it’s how you’ll find out who your true benefactors are. If you feel lost, that’s right: whose youth isn’t lost? I spent the whole day with a fever today. I didn’t take my temperature in the morning, but when I took it in the evening it was 38.5℃. I know I caught a chill on Sunday shooting the short film outdoors in nothing but a thin shirt, and so I came down with a fever. In the afternoon I was reading Liu Tong’s Whose Youth Isn’t Lost, and before I knew it I was in tears. There’s a line in it: when I don’t yet have the ability, all I can do is prove that I’m not afraid of hardship and that I dare to keep going. Because we’re young, we have no choice. So much has happened these past two days. I’m so, so tired, too tired to want to ask about or care about a lot of things anymore. Numbness is slowly filling up my inner world. I once gave myself a hard order. I once said I’d never leave myself a way out, and yet in the end I faced reality and chose the path I’m on now. Restlessness and impatience still show in me. My whole body aches. I’d love to think about happy things more and put my worries behind me. Today I dragged my big head around and spent the day in a daze. I didn’t want to take sick leave, just like my mom, who always works so hard. It hurts inside. I didn’t tell Mom about the fever today. I want to tough it out on my own. I’m afraid she’ll worry, and I’m afraid that if I call her I’ll start crying. All kinds of feelings are mixed up inside me. I’m not that optimistic a person, so I often worry about a lot, and of course I’ve lost a lot too. This is my life. Little by little, you’ll get better. I’ve taken my medicine, and I’m about to go to sleep.

title: Three Years Later
content: From 2010 to 2013, three years just went by like that. Starting, giving up, starting, giving up, and then I started over again. It’s another cold autumn, 16°, and it feels like I’m back in the old days, that age of mine, that way of thinking of mine, yet the world inside me has changed. May God be with you. Amen.

title: Things Change, and You Can Never Outrun Time
content: After all these years, I don’t even know what I’m worrying about anymore. School life is already this exhausting, so I don’t know how I’ll handle what comes after. Won’t it just crush me? Today I called Mom and told her what’s been bothering me. No matter how worried I am, hearing my mother’s comfort and encouragement always takes a weight off my shoulders. Thank you, my wonderful mom. Studying here, I haven’t complained much. I don’t beg anyone to change for me; I just hope I can keep improving. I’m doing fine: three meals a day, a shower at night, a good night’s sleep, a great bunch of classmates, and five roommates who are like family. I thank heaven for giving me this life. Years have gone by, and there are a lot of old classmates I haven’t seen in ages, though I’m still in touch with my close buddies. Today I thought back on the old days, and so, so much of it has faded. Even I have moments when memories slip away, which never used to happen. Thinking it over, I’m 20 now. Time flies, and I’m always way behind it. What goes around comes around; time to pay up. Tonight I listened to Li Zhi’s songs and quietly cried. I don’t want to dwell on the sad stuff. I’ll keep writing my story. To everyone passing by, thanks for watching. Performing on my own stage, forever a lonely actor. Good night, Bengbu. One last thing: Mom, I love you! Thank you! Thank you for letting me pour my heart out. In my next life I want to be your child again, my mom forever.

title: Meeting Again Might Be Easy
content:
These past few days I’ve been sorting through my old connections, trying to find friends I’d lost touch with and their contact info.

Today on QQ I ran into a girl, and I couldn’t remember how we’d met before. We got talking and it turned out we’re from the same place. She’s an elementary school classmate of my childhood best friend. Okay, mind blown.

Meeting again might be easy, and at the same time it isn’t.

Last night I was chatting with an elementary school classmate about our elementary school days, and then I searched for our old homeroom teacher’s name, and I actually found her. At noon the next day I called that school and got through to the principal’s office. I asked, “Does Teacher XX still work at this school?” “She does.” “I’m her former student.” “Do you have her contact information?” “Yes, her office number is XXXXXX, and her cell is XXXXXXX.”

After that I got in touch with my elementary school homeroom teacher. After some small talk, I got her QQ, and I’m planning to hold an elementary school reunion this summer break. I don’t know if it’ll actually happen.

Meeting again is easy. In all my years I’ve rarely left anyone my contact info, and people don’t contact me either, so I’ve lost a lot of connections that way.

Meeting again is easy. If you want to see someone, it really is easy. Unless you don’t want to.

title: Letting Myself Quiet Down and Think Things Through
content:
I’ve been way too busy. Actually, a lot of the time it’s busy for nothing: I don’t do things properly, so it’s really just wasting time

I can’t find the feeling I had a year ago anymore. A year ago I was still a kid, I guess……

Lately I’ve been reading Plato’s The Republic

Its Chinese title is Lixiangguo, “The Ideal State”

Heh~~ it’s the English version, so it’s a bit of a struggle to read~ but it really draws you in. It’s one conversation after another~

I once wrote a post on my QQ Zone called “Everything Tied to Politics Is Ugly”

Then, not long after, I decided that kind of commentary was pointless and deleted it

Yes, it really is pointless. Focus on my own studies and everything else, and walk my own road

I hope I can wander between the nation and the government~ Utopia~~

I recently bought a mouse pad. I didn’t check the model when I bought it, and when it arrived, WOW, it was huge

Uh~~ but it looks pretty cool

Calming down to think is really important for me, I think. That’s what people do~ we think: about what we need to do, and what we can’t do. I have an exam in two weeks, the National Computer Rank Exam Level 2 in C++. It’s a retake, since I failed the written part last time. I’m so bummed. Probably because I only figured out what on earth C++ was a week before the exam~

I used to study C, heh. Last time I got 56 on the written test, just 4 points short. This time I hope to have no regrets. I want to get 80, no regrets. I still have the prep book from last time, so time to review~~

Cheer up! Go, me~ Yes, I Can!

title: We Don't Start from the Same Line
content: We never started from the same line, and yet here we are, thrown together. Ten minutes until lights out in the dorm, so I’ll keep it short. I just want to stress one thing: not everyone in this world is the same as you. There will always be lowly dogs and premiers. So let others do whatever they want. He can be his dog and I’ll be my own person. Everyone has their own ambitions, and forcing people to do what they don’t want isn’t great. Good night to me.

title: Two Tragic Days
content: These past two days have been a real tragedy. I’ve typed this post twice already, because I accidentally closed it before saving. Two days ago, I woke up one morning, opened my site, and it had turned orange, with just one line of English saying: Your account has been suspended. Instantly I was in floods of tears. Why? So I messaged Chenye (a reseller for Qingyun Hosting), only to find he’d gone off on vacation, which made it even more tragic. He said he’d be back on the afternoon of the 16th, and that maybe my site had infringed copyright or used up a lot of the server’s resources. I said there was no way, and so I waited. In the meantime I wanted to buy another host, so I searched on Tencent Weibo and found someone. I told him my host had been suspended over a copyright problem (at the time I didn’t know the reason, I just thought copyright was most likely, so that’s what I told him). Then, right after I said that, he said, we’ve already bought it, we don’t want to add anyone else. I could tell right away, so what more was there to say? The guy just didn’t want the hassle. I told him I’d fix up my blog as required, but he was just one of those people who don’t want any trouble. Fine, no shared hosting then. People these days just don’t want extra hassle. Of course, everyone hates extra hassle…… Speaking of which, my domain is being transferred abroad, to godaddy. 49 yuan to transfer it out, not bad~ I’ve already mailed the paperwork and such to Xinnet’s headquarters in Beijing, but because of the Dragon Boat Festival holiday nobody’s processing it, so I’ll have to wait until tomorrow! Right now I really, really want to buy a host. I think bluehost is the best choice. Going in on a group purchase means sharing one account since you can’t create separate ones, which is bound to cause problems later. Buying it myself costs 330 RMB on Taobao, which scares me off. Now I’m really torn…… If I buy it myself I’ll probably have to wait until September, when I might have some money. The most tragic part is that after my account got suspended I moved to a host in China. I was going to move to Xirang, but Xirang’s bandwidth for the month had run out and the site wouldn’t open, so I moved to Zhujiwu instead. And the very afternoon I finished moving, Zhujiwu went down. Tragic. Zhujiwu still hasn’t recovered………… This afternoon it finally came back. Chenye told me my account had been suspended for using too many server resources, so I checked everything and concluded it was probably the plugins. I’ve now disabled some of them, and I hope there won’t be any more tragedies. Speaking of which, next Tuesday is my academic proficiency test, which is really important for me. Heaven bless me, I studied hard~ Let me get top marks on all of them!!

title: The Blog Turns Two
content: For a long, long time, I disappeared. For the gaokao, I can pick things up and put them down, and I’ve seen through it all. If I have to take the exam, I’ll take it. I chose this, so I’ll give it my best. This site is two years old now, but I’m not in the mood to hold any kind of celebration. A while ago I renewed the domain. I think I’ll just keep renewing it forever. It’ll stay around, the same as me.

title: Chapter 1: Tick-Tock
content:
I’ve been in a much better mood these past few days. First, thank you to the friends who left comments on my last post. I wasn’t able to reply to each of you, but I’m really grateful for your comments. They helped me let go of a lot and figure out a lot of things.

The clock is going tick-tock, so I named this post after that sound. It’s getting colder. This evening a friend I hadn’t seen in months called and asked me out to eat. I said yes, took a shower, and got ready to head out. When I called him again, he said something had come up and I shouldn’t come for now. Fine, back to the computer I went.

This June I took the academic proficiency exams, the ones you need to get your high school diploma. I took them; I remember they lasted three days. People cheated, people used crib sheets. After the exams, I just stayed home the whole time.

Over the summer, apart from one trip to the World Expo, one trip out of town, and one tragic TOEFL test, nothing much happened. Being a super homebody, I mostly hung around the house.

A few days ago I got my hair cut short, and it feels much fresher. Sigh, the reason I cut it short is that I used to have it permed, but now I’m out of money, so I had no choice but to cut it short. Orz…

These past few evenings I’ve been reading Stray Birds, copying out lines. It’s a bilingual edition, and it lets me practice my round-hand lettering too.

My copy of PHP and MySQL Web Development has arrived too, and I’ve started studying. Hehe, I’m aiming to get LuckyBLOG and ShowBLOG online soon!

PS: I learned this Chapter style of writing from Nevermore’s Blog. He’s a student studying abroad (UK) and pretty busy lately. His blog is mostly pictures. If you’ve got time, go leave him a comment on his site, he’ll be happy, hehe. Let me tell you a secret: his nickname is Tragic Little Maruko, because everything he does ends in tragedy. Sigh, now that’s a whole other level! Once again, I recommend Nevermore’s Blog, hehe~

title: What Is Love?
content:
It’s been a long, long time since I wrote anything. Since the first half of last year I’ve hardly written at all. First, there was nothing to write about. Second, I’m lazy. Third, whatever I wrote, only I would read.

What is love? A physiological reaction, without limit or end. (Epigraph) Looking into each other’s eyes, telling the things you find funny, strolling through the city, watching the passersby, walking for miles, talking without ever running out of things to say, then grinning at each other like idiots. I think this is what they call love. I say love is a physiological reaction. Some say it isn’t. Two people meet and fall in love, bodies rubbing together, each completing the other. Tell me, isn’t that a physiological reaction? I say love is a strange phenomenon. Some say it isn’t. Two people meet and fall in love, no words needed, hand in hand. Tell me, isn’t that a strange phenomenon? I say love is an adventurous journey. Some say it isn’t. Two people meet and fall in love, no writing needed, adventuring together. Tell me, isn’t that an adventurous journey? I ask: love, what is it, really? Sex gives us reproduction; God gives us thought. So love is sex sublimated. Love and sex can have nothing to do with each other, or they can. Love can ignore sex, and sex can ignore love. When the two are joined, that’s making love. Platonic love: I think even if I were in the underworld, we could still love each other, because we can set aside the desires of the flesh and pursue something higher of the spirit. Some say this kind of love is just fantasizing, and maybe that’s right, maybe that’s wrong. In a world of flesh and lust, how many people can understand it? A woman’s first time goes to a man, or a woman, or to herself. A man’s first time goes to a woman, or a man, or to himself. Is that loving the other person, or loving yourself? Opposite-sex partners, same-sex partners, partners for life. Great love knows no bounds. I used to say that love can cross borders, cross genders, even cross species. Love can have no limits at all: a feeling of total devotion, a feeling that makes you willing to give up everything, a feeling… Every man wants to be the first man his woman loves, and every woman wants to be the last woman her man loves. That’s what they call love. What is love? Are we trying to explain the meaning of love, or tell her stories? I think the meaning. Since the beginning of time, every single human being has had a love story. With as many people as grains of sand, and as many stories as grains of sand, when could we ever finish telling them all? What is love? She is a long, long epic that can never be fully written or fully told, as if she runs all the way to the far end of humanity. Loving each other isn’t that easy. Everyone has their own temper. Some people want their love to last forever in this world, but the moment you’re gone, your love, just like you, becomes the past, nothing more than an electrical signal flashing across the universe, gliding past without a trace. Some say love is romantic. She certainly is. What is love? There’s no right answer in this world. Love doesn’t need you to say thank you to the other person, but it does need you to give them everything, the happy and the unhappy, the joyful and the joyless, the blissful and the miserable. Love is just that strange. She doesn’t need the other person to remind you, yet the other person can give you exactly what you want. Love: thinking of him, you grin like a fool; thinking of her, you think of every last thing about her. What is love? The love I believe in is just you and me, and then, me and you. PS: I’m going to Shanghai on the 13th, so blog updates will slow down.

title: Where Do I Go from Here?
content:
In this moment of feeling lost, tonight, I put on my headphones and listened to music. On this Saturday night I closed every web page, stopped checking QQ messages, email and code, and started sorting out my thoughts.

Everyone has moments when they feel lost. The feeling lasts until the moment you find hope. I believe this post is the most orderly, most clearly structured thing I’ve written in half a year.

Back at school, I wrote those rambling posts bashing Chinese education. Thinking about it now, is Chinese education really what I care about? No. What I’m thinking about now is how to take my next step well.

I’m writing about myself for the buddies who care about me. I know some people do care, so this post is also an update on how I’ve been.

Right now QQ is flashing again, and I’m ignoring it. In the nearly half a year that’s passed, how many times have I watched QQ flash? In the nearly half a year that’s passed, how many characters have I typed? 551896, according to QQ Pinyin’s stats, and it’s still going up. Over these six months, who kept me company day and night? My laptop. Nobody but it. I have plenty of friends online, yet suddenly I realize how lonely I am. I want to get a hamster, but my parents won’t allow it. Looks like I’ll have to go my own way on this one, but money is a problem. Every month I have to renew several servers, plus my everyday expenses. How am I supposed to manage?

We moved about two years ago. A few days ago my mom told me that a girl from our old neighborhood, the daughter of one of my dad’s coworkers, has leukemia. I never imagined something like this could happen so close to me. She goes to No. 2 High School, she’s in my grade, and her grades are excellent. Fate is cruel and life is unpredictable. Is this what they call the world? I guess so, I think it is. Back in daycare she scratched my face with her fingernails, and I still have the scar……

The next day my grandma was hospitalized. She fell in the early morning and hurt her neck.

My mom says I need to exercise, because I’m a super homebody who’s always holed up at home and never wants to go out. She wants me to go to the gym. I don’t want to; I’ll deal with it later. I’ve been pretty stressed lately, and my chest hurts sometimes. Getting out when I have time would be good for me.

A few days ago, while dropping off a USB drive for a friend, I passed by the gate of my middle school. The Green Fast Food across from the school is gone; it’s a flower shop now. 4 years, time really flies. I still remember 4 years ago, staying after school to do the blackboard bulletin and eating at Green Fast Food. That time is gone, and just like that the people around me all went off to different schools.

The road outside our house still isn’t fixed. They said it would be done before the Tofu Culture Festival (on 9.15), but it still isn’t. It got delayed. Speaking of delays, my plan to study abroad has been delayed too. What does a one-year delay mean? That’s exactly why I feel lost. In this one year I’ve said I’ll finish building the ShowBLOG team, get over 90 on the TOEFL and over 2000 on the SAT. Grand goals, and I don’t know how to reach them. My English is really bad, and it worries me.

My laptop fan is humming away. I haven’t cleaned the dust out in ages; I’ve gotten lazy too. Every day I go to bed at 2 and get up at 10, watch Naruto every Thursday and Detective Conan every Saturday. That’s become my life, and there’s nothing else.

I don’t know what I do with my days. IM? Chatting? Yeah, that’s about it. And the websites, VPS maintenance? Hmm, and newbies asking me questions? I’m getting a bit fed up with that. First, some of it you could find on Google, yet you still ask me. Second, some of it I can’t solve, so it just eats up my time. So from now on, if you have a question, search first, then ask me, preferably by email.

I’ve turned a perfectly good personal indie blog into this mess. Sigh~ it hurts. My personal theme WhiteLove is starting to catch on, and I’m really happy about that, heh. I hope Qiaoqiao sees that last PS, haha. Honestly, I don’t even know who I’m still thinking about now…… Feeling this lost has my head spinning. How could I think about all that?

Watching movies has become my biggest joy. My mom has lots of movie tickets, so whenever I have nothing to do I go to the theater and catch a movie. It adds a little happiness to this dull life of mine.

At this point I’m finding it hard to keep writing. What else is there to say? Seeing Weiwei’s wedding-dress modeling photos gave me a feeling I can’t put into words. I liked her for 4 years, and I still miss her a little. My friends say she isn’t worth it. I say she is. At least I’m not a heartless person. I’m just a coward who can’t face reality and can only regret.

Three years ago, while I was studying for the high school entrance exam, every night on my way home from cram school I’d cross a pedestrian bridge. There was an old man there playing the erhu. He was blind and begging there. Every time I passed, I gave him all the change in my pocket. I just felt he was different from other beggars. He relied entirely on his own effort; his music was his work, and that’s why I gave him money. I really can’t stand beggars who kneel on the ground without moving. You’re not disabled, so why are you lying there playing dead? The day before yesterday, after visiting my grandma at the hospital, I passed that spot again and saw the old man, and I still emptied my pocket and gave him the money. I once thought about using what my websites earn for charity, but my means really are small, so I’ll leave that for later. When I see someone on the street who needs help, I can still go and help.

The ShowBLOG team is now fully assembled and has started development on the project. I hope everything goes smoothly from here. I’m treating this as a project for going abroad, and I want to do it well, so that it, this whole family of sites, can stand out among websites in China and around the world and become well-known. I’ll keep my feet on the ground and do it one step at a time. Wish me luck, everyone.

Delaying going abroad by a year puts a lot of pressure on me. I’ve said it before: when you’re all sophomores, I’ll just be a freshman. I don’t know how I’ll face my classmates at next year’s graduation photo. I don’t want to go, but that would be a regret, a regret for the rest of my life……

Lately I think I could read some poetry. Living on the internet, I’ve run a bit short of words, and I need books to fill myself back up. I’m a bit worn out by coding books where one is one and two is two. Reading something literary and sorting out my thoughts, how pleasant that would be.

I’ve been watching some videos lately, and I don’t think I need to have any objections to Chinese society. I live here, and I’m still a Chinese citizen. In the future I hope I can get Hong Kong citizenship and US citizenship (dual citizenship). The mainland doesn’t allow dual citizenship because of its national circumstances, so there’s nothing I can do to make the mainland change. I just need to change myself.

Changing myself is where I’m headed from now on. When things aren’t going my way, I’ll try changing myself: my position, my way of thinking, how I divide up my interests, and so on, and not worry about other people or the country.

Where do I go from here?

Write my own story down, read it back to myself, then make a plan from it, and I think my life will be perfect.

I’ve said it before: I want a perfect life. I need to taste all the “flavors” of life and “eat my fill,” heh. I hope I can face everything with a smile and keep going bravely.

I’m planning to quit IM or switch accounts and start a new journey. I’m going to put my old QQ number on hold for a while.

I forgot to mention, someone gave me a pair of couple QQ numbers, and I don’t know who to give the other one to. People in IT can’t find girlfriends, and I’ll say it, that’s right: I lack a sense of humor, I’m not good at talking to girls, I dodge and hide. Someone who can’t stand himself, how could he possibly…… The tragedy of being single buys you freedom, and you can be lazy about doing things, haha. That’s the part I like best.

My ears are getting tired from the headphones, and this post is about to end. 2000-some characters, not bad.

Where do I go from here?

What I want to say is, I walk my own path. Everyone else, let them talk. We’re not on the same path. No two people walk the same path; they can be similar, never identical.

Starting today I’m going to study my English books properly and memorize vocabulary. IM is wasting a bit of my time. I’m switching to a new account, which I’ve already announced, or just email me.

OK, that’s it for now. Where do I go from here? I walk my own path.

title: I Asked, What Is Freedom? He Said: Dogs are Freedom
content:
This morning the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology called me (I was still asleep) and told me to delete a certain post (a really bad post, apparently only because it ranked fairly high in search engines). I did as I was told, so as not to get into trouble, but I still wasn’t happy about it, and so came the piece below.

Quite an honor, too: the first time I’ve been put on their radar.

Here’s a short piece

English:

I asked, what is freedom?

This place is not freedom

I said: freedom does not belong to this place

He said: We are freedom

You said: We do not need freedom

They said: Freedom is not belong to you

“They” said: dogs are freedom

I said: I am not a dog

He said: I am not a dog

You said: I wish I were a dog

They said: I am a dog, not human

“They” said: Dogs are not freedom

I said: I want my freedom

He said: I want your freedom

They said: We want our freedom

“They” said: Arrest them! Under house arrest them! Shoot them!

I said: I give up freedom

He said: I give up freedom

They said: we give up freedom

“They” said: I give dogs to freedom and will not give you to freedom

Finally, Dogs are freedom

 

Chinese:

I asked, what is freedom?

There is no freedom in this place

I said: freedom does not belong to this place

He said: we are free

You said: we don’t need freedom

They said: freedom does not belong to you

“They” said: freedom belongs to dogs

I said: I am not a dog

He said: I am not a dog either

You said: I wish I were a dog

They said: I’d rather be a dog than a human

“They” said: dogs have no right to freedom either

I said: I want my freedom

He said: I want your freedom

They said: we want our freedom

“They” said: arrest them, put them under house arrest, shoot them!

I said: I give up my right to freedom

He said: I give up my right to freedom too

They said: we give up our right to freedom

“They” said: I give dogs the right to freedom, and I will not give it to you

At last, the dogs had freedom

Note: I won’t say more, and I won’t explain. If you get it, you get it. If you don’t, I won’t explain. It’s pretty simple. The post is deleted, and yours truly has gone quiet. Who knows, one of these days I might end up just like what I wrote above… Friends leaving comments, watch what you say… the review period might not be over yet… A sad country… and I still have to stay here another two years… What a total tragedy…

title: An Update on Things Lately
content: My plan to study abroad has been canceled. There are a lot of reasons, so I won’t go into exactly why. These past two years were like the ocean, and then suddenly a meteorite crashed into it and threw everything into chaos. Of course my dream is still there, and I have to keep going. There’s nothing much to celebrate at Christmas. I’m on my own, and I still feel so lonely. It’s cold and bleak. Finally, Merry Christmas, everyone. Next year I need to prepare seriously for the gaokao, the college entrance exam, so I’ll have less and less time to chat with you all about blogs.

title: Colder Than December
content:
It’s 6:22 a.m. Beijing time, December 9, 2013. My alarm woke me up early so I could get to school for the flag-raising ceremony, because today is December 9th, the anniversary of the 1935 student movement. Outside there’s smog and a strong wind, and I’m not sure I’ll even be able to catch a bus to school. My body has been pretty worn out lately, just like me last year as a freshman, not knowing anything but plowing away like a water buffalo, maybe for the sake of the future. I hope the effort isn’t wasted.

Effort

For nearly two years now I’ve been fighting for that one word. May hard work be rewarded.

content:

title: New Blood in the WordPress China Community
content:
A few days ago CN WORDPRESS changed hands. (I’ve confirmed he’s a middle school graduate. Sigh, now I feel like I’ve missed so many opportunities, so much time.) Apparently the new guy is a high school student, or a middle school student, or a college student, not sure about his age, most likely a high school student, whatever~ Anyway, he’s not someone with a job, Great, the once lifeless CN WORDPRESS finally has some energy. His taking over might well bring WordPress in China back to life~ o(∩_∩)o haha

Him: Zheng Jiehan (a new high school freshman). I don’t know him, but I bow down to him. He’s taken on the heavy job of releasing updates for CN WORDPRESS. Thanks to him. Paveo, who did it before, also deserves respect.

The official Chinese WORDPRESS 3.0.1 update is out. I waited a long, long time…

There’s also a WordPress 3.0.1 supplementary language pack update. That’s the new energy for you~

I really did get into building websites late. What was I doing in seventh grade? In eighth grade? In ninth grade? Sigh, what a tragedy, so much time just slipped away. The person localizing WORDPRESS and taking it over is a middle schooler. Ugh, I feel so inferior…

Sigh, it was always my mom holding me back, not giving me money to build a site. Only in 2010 did I finally get some money, and that’s when I built my site. I got into this so, so late. Sigh, really. I’ve missed a lot of chances, and now I can only make up for it with hard work.

Finally, thanks to Zheng Jiehan for bringing new energy to CN WORDPRESS. Another tech whiz. Thanks for all your hard work.

PS: Speaking of which, I’m learning C++, so why does it feel like there’s nowhere to use it… At my level I’d never make it into NOIP…

Updated January 3, 2015:

Later it changed hands again, to someone who seems to be his friend. Looks like he’s abroad now too.

title: A Quick Roundup of My Blog Plugins
content:
I’ve had my own self-hosted blog for about 6 months now, and so far I haven’t posted anything about tinkering with wordpress. So let me talk about the plugins my wordpress uses.

Here’s my plugin list, in alphabetical order, with download links:

Akismet Blocks spam comments. No need to say more about this one~

All in One SEO Pack SEO optimization. Tons of people say you need it, tons of people say you don’t, uh~ I’m confused~ so I’ve never removed it

Comment Info Detector Shows each commenter’s location, browser and operating system. Very cool. I’m using a modified version

Clean Archives Reloaded A very handy plugin for displaying post archives

Delete-Revision Deletes redundant post revisions. Very useful. You don’t need to keep it enabled, just clean things up every so often

Executable PHP widget Lets you add PHP code directly in sidebar widgets. Very handy, though also a bit of a “nice but not really needed” thing

Fluency Admin An admin dashboard makeover plugin, recommended by the BOSS of SHOWBLOG. Once you use it, your dashboard looks really slick!

Google XML Sitemaps Google sitemap generator. This one is a must!

Hacklog Highslide Picture A modified image display plugin

Highslide4WP Enhances emoticons in comments

Highslide for Wordpress reloaded Image zoom plugin

Mail To Commenter Email replies to comments. Since my blog theme doesn’t support threaded comments, this one is great, and it keeps users coming back!

NextGEN Gallery Photo gallery. It’s too bloated, so it’s turned off for now and I’m using a different gallery

OpenID Not enabled for regular users yet. It lets people log in quickly. I recommend reading this post by Lanbing

Page Links To Makes a page link straight to another URL. Very handy, no need to edit the source code

Post Layout Ad insertion plugin. Makes it easy to insert ads into posts

SyntaxHighlighter Evolved A very powerful code plugin, though my blog also has a built-in code plugin

Thumbnail For Excerpts Plugin for showing thumbnails, disabled for now

Wibiya Toolbar Very cool tools, removed for now

WordPress Mobile Pack Plugin for mobile access

WordPress Related Posts Related posts plugin. Master willin’s version can do this too, a modified version by zwwooooo

wp-comment-warrior Top commenters list, disabled for now

WP-Cumulus Tag cloud with Chinese support. I’ve optimized it to support Chinese text and the YaHei font, with no jittering. The original version doesn’t support Chinese, and some versions jitter. Here’s the download link for the 3D tag cloud: click here to download from 115 cloud drive

WP-MulticolLinks Splits the blogroll into columns so the links don’t take up a lot of space. CSS could do this too, but I’m lazy

WP-PageNavi Pagination plugin. It improves on wordpress’s default pagination

WP-reCAPTCHA Comment CAPTCHA plugin. It’s way too powerful, so I don’t dare use it. People would curse me out if I did

WP-RecentComments Sidebar recent comments plugin, with ajax enabled, mainly to go with my theme

WPVN - Username Changer Plugin for changing the super admin username, mainly for 2.9.2. You don’t need it in 3.0

That’s it. I’m still on 2.9.2, so there aren’t many compatibility problems and everything works fine. Some plugins might have issues in 3.0. Let’s all share what we find~

10.09.2015 update

It’s rare for me to look back like this. I used wordpress for so long, and I really miss these plugins

title: A 3D Tag Cloud Plugin for WordPress: WP Cumulus
content:
I think this has to be the coolest tag cloud effect I’ve ever seen: a super flashy WordPress tag cloud built with Flash+JS. I only found it while aimlessly browsing, clicking one link after another until I ended up there. Turns out something like this exists, and it’s well worth recommending. What does it look like? Check out my sidebar. Best of all, the version I’m using fully supports Chinese!

Main features of the WP Cumulus ****WordPress plugin:

  1. The cloud can contain tags or categories, or both.
  2. Supports widgets and custom template code.
  3. Doesn’t affect search engine crawling. The tag cloud it generates is only displayed visually as 3D Flash, but the source code it produces is the same as WordPress’s default tag cloud. If you don’t have Adobe Flash Player ActiveX installed, it just shows up as an ordinary tag list.

How to use the WP Cumulus WordPress plugin:

  1. Upload and activate it.
  2. Click Appearance, then Widgets. A list of available widgets will appear; pick WP-Cumulus from it.
  3. Drag WP-Cumulus into the sidebar next to it and configure it.

  • Since the settings screen can’t be translated into Chinese (a character encoding problem), I can only give translations of the English here. Width and height set the size it’s displayed at in the sidebar

  • Tag color, second color, highlight color, background color, and whether the background is transparent: just set these to match your theme!

  • Rotation speed. This version of WP-Cumulus has been modified, so it doesn’t have the jittery rotation some versions of WP-Cumulus floating around online have. It spins very smoothly

  • Whether the tags are spread evenly over the sphere: change this to suit your situation~

  • Tags, categories, or both: where the displayed items come from. Set this one to suit your situation too~

  • The last option takes wp_tag_cloud parameters, which let you set things like how many tags the cloud shows and the largest and smallest font sizes. Of course some parameters can’t take effect, such as orderby, order and so on

    The effect WP Cumulus creates really is great. Put a Flash tag cloud like this on your blog and it’s guaranteed to catch visitors’ eyes. Best of all, WP-Cumulus only loads a 7KB swf, so it definitely won’t slow down your page load! Beauty and speed? A perfect match!
